classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: etendue_of_bolometer
items.description:
Geometric optical throughput of a bolometer channel, equal to the product of
its effective collecting area and accepted solid angle.
items.documentation:
Étendue is the geometric optical throughput of a bolometer channel: the
phase-space acceptance of rays transmitted from the viewed region to the
detector. It determines how radiance is converted into collected optical
power.

For a uniform angular acceptance, the étendue is defined by

$$
G = A\Omega
$$

where $G$ is the étendue, $A$ is the effective collecting area, and $\Omega$
is the accepted solid angle. For nonuniform acceptance, $G$ denotes the
corresponding integral over the projected collecting area and accepted
directions.

The quantity describes optical throughput only; detector conversion
efficiency and electronic response are separate properties. It is the
channel-level counterpart of [line-of-sight
étendue](name:etendue_of_line_of_sight) and is closely related to the
aperture area defined by [diagnostic aperture
area](name:area_of_diagnostic_aperture).

items.name: runaway_electron_current_density
items.description:
Runaway-electron current density is the vector density of conventional
electric charge flux carried by suprathermal electrons beyond the
collisional drag limit.
items.documentation:
Runaway-electron current density $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the vector
density of conventional electric charge flux carried by suprathermal
electrons beyond the collisional drag limit. Because electron charge is
negative, its direction is opposite to the net runaway-electron particle
flux.

It is defined by the charge-weighted first velocity moment of the
runaway-electron distribution:

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{RE}}(\mathbf{x},t)=q_e\int_{\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{RE}}}\mathbf{v}\,f_e(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $q_e$ is electron charge,
$\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, $f_e$ is the electron velocity-space
distribution, and $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the velocity-space subset
beyond the collisional drag limit.

As a population-restricted form of [current density](name:current_density),
it excludes thermal and nonrunaway electrons, ion contributions, and
displacement-current density. The vector precedes geometric projection and
volume averaging; its field-aligned projection is [parallel runaway-electron
current density](name:parallel_runaway_electron_current_density), while
volume-averaged runaway-electron current density represents its volume
average. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, components are
projections onto the corresponding basis directions.

Sign convention: Positive when a stated component or scalar projection of
$\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ aligns with the positive direction of its
defining basis vector or unit vector.

items.name: accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Cumulative post-breakdown carbon inventory from gas injection, expressed as
six equivalent-electron counts for every injected neutral carbon atom.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative post-breakdown inventory of carbon atoms
delivered by gas injection, represented as an equivalent-electron count. It
excludes carbon introduced during the plasma prefill phase and does not
represent an instantaneous source rate or a charge-state-resolved ion
inventory.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{C,eq}}(t)=6N_{\mathrm{C}}(t)=6\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C}}^{\mathrm{gas}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{C,eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{C}}$
is the cumulative number of injected carbon atoms,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C}}^{\mathrm{gas}}$ is the carbon injection rate,
$t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma breakdown time, and $t$ is the evaluation
time. The factor 6 is carbon's atomic number. This is the post-breakdown
component of carbon count due to gas injection and is distinct from [carbon
prefill count due to gas
injection](name:carbon_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection).

items.name: ion_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam
items.description:
Ion absorbed power of a beam-tracing beam is the electromagnetic wave power
transferred from a single coherent beam to a selected ion species along its
trajectory.
items.documentation:
The ion absorbed power of a beam-tracing beam is the total electromagnetic
wave power transferred from a single coherent beam to one selected ion
species along the beam trajectory. It is a species-resolved contribution to
the [absorbed power of a beam-tracing
beam](name:absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam), distinct from the electron
contribution represented by [electron absorbed power of a beam-tracing
beam](name:electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam).

The species partition of the beam power balance is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs}} = P_e + \sum_s P_{\mathrm{ion},s}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the total absorbed beam power, $P_e$ is the
electron contribution, $P_{\mathrm{ion},s}$ is the power absorbed by ion
species $s$, and the sum is over the contributing ion species. This quantity
denotes one term $P_{\mathrm{ion},s}$; its charge-state-resolved counterpart
is [ion charge-state absorbed power of a beam-tracing
beam](name:ion_charge_state_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam). It
excludes residual wave power represented by power of a beam-tracing beam and
differs from volume-integrated [ion absorbed wave
power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power).

items.name: carbon_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory introduced as carbon gas during
plasma prefill, with six count units assigned to each injected carbon atom.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of carbon
introduced by gas injection during the plasma prefill phase, before plasma
breakdown. It represents injected carbon atoms rather than an instantaneous
injection rate.

The defining relation is

$$
N_{\mathrm{C,eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{C}}N_{\mathrm{C}} = 6N_{\mathrm{C}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{C,eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{C}}$
is the cumulative number of injected carbon atoms, and $Z_{\mathrm{C}}=6$ is
the carbon atomic number. Both counts are dimensionless.

The prefill interval ends at plasma breakdown, so post-breakdown carbon
delivery is represented separately by [accumulated carbon count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection). The
aggregation convention parallels [accumulated hydrogen prefill
count](name:accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count), with the atomic number
providing the equivalent-electron weighting.

items.name: neutral_state_energy_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless coefficient that limits the energy flux density of neutrals in
a specified internal state relative to its collisionless free-streaming
bound.
items.documentation:
The energy-flux limiter coefficient for a specified neutral internal state
is a dimensionless factor that sets the maximum allowed energy flux density
carried by that state relative to its collisionless free-streaming bound.

The limiting relation is

$$
|q_E| \leq \alpha_E q_{E,\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $q_E$ is the energy flux density carried by neutrals in the specified
internal state, $\alpha_E$ is this energy-flux limiter coefficient, and
$q_{E,\mathrm{fs}}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming
energy-flux bound.

The coefficient applies only to energy transport by the specified neutral
internal state; it is not summed over other neutral internal states and does
not limit ion, electron, momentum, or particle flux. It is the neutral-state
specialization of the broader [energy flux-limiter
coefficient](name:energy_flux_limiter_coefficient). The related [neutral
momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) has the same
neutral-particle scope but limits momentum-flux density rather than
energy-flux density.

items.name: energy_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Energy flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor that scales the
collisionless free-streaming upper bound on population-resolved energy flux
density while preserving its direction.
items.documentation:
Energy flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor that scales a
collisionless free-streaming upper bound on population-resolved energy flux
density in a transport closure. It limits the permitted magnitude while
preserving the direction or sign assigned by the underlying closure.

For a resolved energy-flux channel, the limited flux is defined by:

$$
F_E = \operatorname{sgn}\!\left(F_E^{\mathrm{cl}}\right)\min\!\left(\left|F_E^{\mathrm{cl}}\right|, L_E F_E^{\mathrm{fs}}\right)
$$

where $F_E$ is the limited energy flux density, the subscript $E$ identifies
the energy channel, $F_E^{\mathrm{cl}}$ is the unconstrained closure value,
$F_E^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the corresponding positive collisionless
free-streaming bound, $L_E$ is the energy flux limiter coefficient, and
$\operatorname{sgn}$ is the sign function. The limiter convention uses $0
\leq L_E \leq 1$, with smaller values imposing a stricter cap.

This parent covers energy-flux limiting for either an ion population or a
neutral population resolved by internal state. For ions, the energy flux is
aggregated by summing contributions over all ion charge states; for
neutrals, the coefficient applies to the specified internal state rather
than to an unspecified sum over states. No particular spatial region or
directional component is imposed by this parent.

The coefficient is not the energy flux density, its collisionless bound, or
the unconstrained closure value; it specifies only the multiplicative
limiting factor. It does not describe momentum-flux limiting, which is
represented by the distinct [momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

This quantity is the energy-flux specialization of the general [flux limiter
coefficient](name:flux_limiter_coefficient). Its concrete instances include
the charge-state-summed [ion energy flux limiter
coefficient](name:ion_energy_flux_limiter_coefficient) and the
internal-state-resolved [neutral-state energy flux limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_state_energy_flux_limiter_coefficient).

items.name: opacity_at_ece_channel_emission_position
items.description:
Dimensionless optical depth along the electron-cyclotron-emission viewing
path at a channel emission position, indicating whether the detected
emission is local and thermal.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the optical depth of the plasma evaluated at the emission
position associated with one electron-cyclotron-emission channel. It
measures the cumulative attenuation between the emitting region and the
relevant observation path.

The optical depth is defined by

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{ECE}}(s_{\mathrm{em}}) = \int_{\mathcal{P}(s_{\mathrm{em}})} \alpha_{\mathrm{ECE}}(s)\,ds
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{ECE}}$ is the electron-cyclotron-emission optical
depth, $s_{\mathrm{em}}$ is the channel emission position,
$\mathcal{P}(s_{\mathrm{em}})$ is the line-of-sight path used to accumulate
the optical depth at that position, $\alpha_{\mathrm{ECE}}$ is the
electron-cyclotron-emission absorption coefficient, and $s$ is distance
along that path.

The scope is one channel and its associated emission position; values are
not summed or averaged over channels or over emission positions. This
quantity is the accumulated optical depth, not the local absorption
coefficient or a channel-integrated aggregate. It is the position-specific
form of [opacity](name:opacity), with the evaluation locus made explicit.

Optical depth greater than one indicates optically thick, locally thermal
emission, whereas optical depth less than one indicates that non-local or
suprathermal contributions can be important.

items.name: deuterium_tritium_emissivity_due_to_fusion
items.description:
Local volumetric rate of neutron production from deuterium-tritium fusion
reactions, giving the spatial distribution of D-T neutron emission per unit
volume at each point in the plasma.
items.documentation:
The deuterium-tritium neutron emissivity $\varepsilon_{DT}$ is the local
number of neutrons produced per unit volume per unit time from D-T fusion
reactions. Each D-T fusion reaction produces exactly one neutron, so this
quantity is equal to the local D-T fusion reaction-rate density.

For reacting deuterium and tritium ion populations, the emissivity is given
by:

$$
\varepsilon_{DT} = n_D \, n_T \, \langle \sigma v \rangle_{DT}
$$

where $n_D$ and $n_T$ are the local deuterium and tritium number densities
and $\langle \sigma v \rangle_{DT}$ is the D-T fusion reactivity, the
velocity-averaged fusion cross-section evaluated over the relative-velocity
distribution of the reacting ion populations; for thermal reactants it is
the thermally averaged reactivity at the local ion temperature. No symmetry
factor appears because the reactants are distinct species.

This quantity counts neutron production, not fusion energy deposition or
neutron power. It is the D-T channel of the parent emissivity_due_to_fusion
and the counterpart of
[deuterium_deuterium_emissivity_due_to_fusion](name:deuterium_deuterium_emissivity_due_to_fusion),
which covers the neutron-emitting D-D branch. Its energy-weighted
counterpart is
[deuterium_tritium_power_density_due_to_fusion](name:deuterium_tritium_power_density_due_to_fusion),
and integrating the emissivity over the plasma volume and weighting by the
per-reaction neutron energy connects to the total_neutron_power.

items.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate of coherent-wave energy transfer to
fast, nonthermal ions of a selected species, summed over ionic charge states
and resolved by toroidal Fourier mode.
items.documentation:
Toroidal-mode-resolved fast-ion power density is the flux-surface-averaged
rate at which an individual toroidal wave harmonic transfers energy to the
nonthermal fast-ion population of a selected species per unit physical
volume. It describes direct coherent-wave absorption, not subsequent
collisional redistribution of the absorbed energy.

For each toroidal harmonic, the averaged deposition density is defined by

$$
p_{i,\mathrm{f}}(n_\phi) = \left\langle \frac{dE_{i,\mathrm{f}}(n_\phi)}{dt\,dV} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $p_{i,\mathrm{f}}(n_\phi)$ is the mode-resolved fast-ion power
density, $i$ labels the selected ion species, $\mathrm{f}$ identifies its
fast population, $n_\phi$ is the integer toroidal Fourier mode number, and
$E_{i,\mathrm{f}}(n_\phi)$ is the energy transferred by that harmonic to
this population. Here $t$ is time, $V$ is physical volume, and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes averaging over the magnetic flux
surface.

The species contribution is summed over all ionic charge states, but not
over different ion species or toroidal harmonics. The [charge-state-resolved
counterpart](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density)
separates the contributions whose sum gives this species-level quantity.
Thermal ions and electrons are excluded. The flux-surface average is
distinct from the unaveraged local deposition density and is not a
volume-integrated power.

Summing over a complete, consistently normalized set of toroidal harmonics
recovers the flux-surface-averaged [fast-ion power
density](name:fast_ion_power_density). Integrating the averaged density over
an enclosed physical volume gives the corresponding [mode-resolved fast-ion
absorbed wave power](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_absorbed_wave_power).
Each harmonic contribution is an absorbed power density, not a Fourier
amplitude of the deposited-power distribution.

Sign convention: Positive when energy is transferred from the coherent wave
to the fast-ion population.

items.name: counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Collisional counter-passing torque density for fast ions is the local vector
rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit volume caused by Coulomb
collisions.
items.documentation:
Collisional counter-passing torque density for fast ions is the local source
density of angular momentum transferred to or from the counter-passing
fast-ion population by Coulomb collisions. It retains the full
torque-density vector rather than resolving it along one direction.

The vector quantity is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{cp,fast}} = \left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}^{\mathrm{cp,fast}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{cp,fast}}$ is the
collisional torque-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\ell}^{\mathrm{cp,fast}}$ is
the local angular-momentum density of counter-passing fast ions, and $t$ is
time. This quantity provides the vector parent for the [toroidal
counter-passing fast-ion torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
and complements the toroidal sibling [toroidal fast-ion torque density due
to collisions](name:toroidal_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions). It
is a local source density, not a volume-integrated torque, and belongs to
the broader [fast-ion torque density due to
collisions](name:fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when the radial, toroidal, or vertical component
points in the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

items.name: toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of xenon ions, averaged over
all ionization states at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport
barrier.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity
at the H-mode pedestal top. It is the density-weighted mean over all xenon
ionization states, rather than a sum of their velocities.

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Xe},q} V_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe},q}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Xe},q}}
$$

Here $q$ labels xenon ionization state, $n_{\mathrm{Xe},q}$ is the number
density of that state, and $V_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe},q}$ is its toroidal
bulk-flow component. The denominator is the total xenon ion density
corresponding to xenon density at the pedestal top. The value is evaluated
at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier and is
distinct from [toroidal xenon velocity at the internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier) and
[toroidal xenon velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

Sign convention: Positive when the velocity component along $\hat{\phi}$ is
positive in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: helium_3_density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Number density of helium-3 ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary, summed over positive ionization states and
excluding neutral helium-3 atoms.
items.documentation:
Number density of helium-3 ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the helium-3-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local helium-3 number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_3 = \frac{dN_3}{dV}
$$

where $n_3$ is the helium-3 ion number density, $N_3$ is the number of
helium-3 ions in a small plasma volume, and $V$ is that plasma volume. The
count $N_3$ includes singly ionized and fully stripped helium-3 ions.

This quantity applies to the helium-3 ion population immediately upstream of
the electrostatic sheath at a divertor target. It is summed over the
positive ionization states of helium-3, excludes neutral helium-3 atoms, and
excludes electrons and all other ion species.

Unlike
[helium_4_density_at_divertor_target](name:helium_4_density_at_divertor_target),
this quantity describes the isotope with three nucleons. Unlike
[helium_3_density_at_limiter](name:helium_3_density_at_limiter), it is
evaluated at a divertor target rather than at a limiter surface.

items.name: toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Density-weighted mean toroidal fluid-velocity component of all tritium ion
charge states at the internal transport barrier, directed along increasing
toroidal angle.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the density-weighted mean of the toroidal fluid-velocity
component for all tritium ions at the internal transport barrier. It
excludes neutral tritium and aggregates the ionic charge states.

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{T}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{T},q} v_{\phi,\mathrm{T},q}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{T},q}}
$$

Here $q$ indexes tritium ionic charge states, $n_{\mathrm{T},q}$ is the
corresponding number density in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{T},q}$ is the
toroidal fluid-velocity component in m s$^{-1}$. The denominator is the
total tritium-ion density, related to [tritium density at the internal
transport barrier](name:tritium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier). The
internal transport barrier is the flux-surface location where cross-field
transport is locally reduced and kinetic gradients are steep; this quantity
is distinct from the corresponding value at the [magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

Sign convention: Positive when the density-weighted tritium-ion velocity
component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: electron_temperature_at_limiter
items.description:
Kinetic temperature of the electron population evaluated at the
plasma-facing side of a limiter, where open scrape-off-layer field lines
terminate.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local kinetic temperature of the electron population at
the plasma-wall interface on the plasma-facing side of a limiter, where open
scrape-off-layer field lines terminate. It is the electron-specific member
of temperature at limiter.

For an isotropic electron population, its temperature expressed in energy
units is defined by

$$
T_e = \frac{2}{3}\langle E_{\mathrm{kin},e} \rangle
$$

where $T_e$ is the electron kinetic temperature and $\langle
E_{\mathrm{kin},e} \rangle$ is the mean random kinetic energy per electron.

The quantity refers to electrons on the plasma-facing side of the limiter
interface and does not denote the temperature of the limiter material. It is
distinct from the density-weighted population average average temperature at
limiter, which combines the relevant plasma populations.

items.name: inner_radius_of_correction_coil
items.description:
Inner radius of a correction coil is the non-negative distance from the
center of an annular non-axisymmetric correction-coil conductor
cross-section to its inner circular boundary.
items.documentation:
Inner radius of a correction coil is the non-negative distance from the
center of an annular non-axisymmetric correction-coil conductor or
winding-pack cross-section to its inner circular boundary. It defines the
bore size of the annular material region.

This quantity applies only to correction-coil cross-sections whose geometry
is annular. It is a local cross-sectional geometric distance for the
conductor or winding pack, not an aggregation over multiple coils or turns.

It is distinct from the correction-coil centerline position, from any
major-radius coordinate of the coil in space, from the outer cross-sectional
radius, and from the material cross-sectional area. It describes the inner
hole boundary, not the amount of conductor material.

For an annular correction-coil cross-section, this inner radius complements
the corresponding correction-coil radius in specifying the radial bounds of
the annulus. The [area of a correction coil](name:area_of_correction_coil)
is a related cross-sectional quantity, but its definition is
geometry-dependent and is not generally determined by this inner radius
alone.

items.name: total_particle_count
items.description:
Total number of particles in the kinetic distribution, obtained by
integrating the distribution function over velocity space and the entire
plasma volume.
items.documentation:
The total particle count is the global normalization integral of the
particle distribution function $f(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{v})$: it quantifies
the total number of particles of the described species present in the plasma
at a given instant, summed over all spatial positions within the plasma
volume and all velocities in phase space. Being a pure count, it is
dimensionless.

The quantity is defined by the phase-space integral

$$
N = \int_V \int f(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{v}) \, d^3v \, d^3x
$$

where $V$ is the plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is the position vector, and
$\mathbf{v}$ is the particle velocity. In marker-based kinetic simulations,
$N$ reduces to the weighted sum over all simulation markers.

Monitoring $N$ over time provides a particle-conservation diagnostic in
kinetic modeling: systematic drift from the initial value indicates
numerical particle sources or losses. This quantity is closely related to
total_count, which carries the same physical meaning with a less
species-explicit name, and contrasts with
[fast_count](name:total_fast_particle_count), which integrates only over the
non-thermal sub-population of the distribution. The local spatial
counterpart is total_particle_density, whose volume integral recovers $N$.

items.name: z_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid
items.description:
Vertical Z coordinate of the geometric centroid of a ferritic element in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where Z increases upward from the
machine midplane.
items.documentation:
The vertical coordinate $Z_\mathrm{cent}$ specifies the height of the
geometric centroid of a ferritic element along the $Z$-axis of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is the major radius
from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle increasing
counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is the vertical
height measured from the machine midplane.

Ferritic elements are passive ferromagnetic components installed in some
tokamak configurations to reduce toroidal magnetic field ripple generated by
discrete toroidal field coils. The centroid position serves as the
representative reference point for each element in electromagnetic field
models that compute the perturbed equilibrium field arising from the
ferromagnetic material. Together with
[radial_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid](name:radial_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid),
this coordinate fully determines the axisymmetric centroid location in the
poloidal $(R, Z)$ plane.

For configurations requiring the full three-dimensional centroid location,
the Cartesian counterparts
[x_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid](name:x_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid)
and
[y_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid](name:y_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid)
provide the transverse displacement when the element's toroidal position is
also needed. Centroid coordinates are derived from the engineering design
geometry of the device and used as inputs to equilibrium reconstruction and
ripple-compensation analyzes.

Sign convention: Positive when the centroid lies above the machine midplane
in the $+Z$ direction.

items.name: toroidal_total_momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Effective Fickian coefficient relating the diffusive flux of aggregated
toroidal momentum to its local toroidal momentum-density gradient.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the effective Fickian transport coefficient for the
diffusive part of the total toroidal-momentum flux. It applies to the
toroidal momentum component in the total momentum balance, not to a toroidal
transport direction.

For an outward flux-surface-normal coordinate $\ell$, the local diffusive
closure is:

$$
\Gamma_{\phi,\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\phi,\mathrm{tot}}\,\frac{\partial M_{\phi,\mathrm{tot}}}{\partial \ell}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\phi,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the outward diffusive flux density of
total toroidal momentum, $D_{\phi,\mathrm{tot}}$ is this effective
diffusivity, $M_{\phi,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the aggregated toroidal momentum
density, and $\ell$ is distance in the outward flux-surface-normal
direction. The minus sign specifies down-gradient diffusive transport.

The aggregation is over the momentum contributions represented in the total
momentum balance. This quantity excludes convective transport and the total
momentum flux itself; it is a coefficient multiplying the gradient of
toroidal momentum rather than a flux or velocity.

It is the toroidal component specialization of [total momentum
diffusivity](name:total_momentum_diffusivity). The corresponding poloidal
specialization, [poloidal total momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_total_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), applies
the same Fickian closure to the poloidal momentum component.

items.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Effective kinematic coefficient relating diffusive transport of toroidal
momentum in a specified ion species and charge state to its opposing
momentum-density gradient.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective kinematic coefficient governing diffusive
redistribution of toroidal [momentum](name:momentum) carried by ions of one
specified species and charge state. Toroidal denotes the direction of
increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

In a local directional Fick-law closure, the coefficient is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{s,\phi}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\chi_{s,\phi}\frac{\partial g_{s,\phi}}{\partial \ell}
$$

where $s$ identifies the specified ion species and charge state,
$\Pi_{s,\phi}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux of toroidal momentum
along the selected transport direction, $\chi_{s,\phi}$ is this diffusivity,
$g_{s,\phi}$ is the toroidal momentum density, and $\ell$ is physical
distance increasing along that transport direction. The momentum density is
$g_{s,\phi}=m_s n_s v_{s,\phi}$, where $m_s$ is the ion mass, $n_s$ is the
charge-state number density, and $v_{s,\phi}$ is the charge-state mean
toroidal velocity.

This is the toroidal-momentum component of [ion charge-state momentum
diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity). The toroidal
qualifier selects the transported momentum component, not the direction of
its flux or gradient; it does not require transport along a toroidal arc.
The coefficient is resolved for one charge state, without summation or
averaging over charge states. It excludes the advective contribution
represented by [toroidal ion charge-state momentum convection
velocity](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity),
residual stress, and external momentum sources.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_geometric_axis
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of the plasma boundary's geometric axis, equal to
its perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Major-radius coordinate of geometric axis

The coordinate is defined by

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal coordinates of the same reference
position in the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame, with $z$ the
vertical coordinate along the same axis as $Z$.

This nonnegative coordinate specifies one reference position associated with
the plasma boundary, rather than separate positions for interior flux
surfaces. It is not a minor radius or a magnetic flux label, and it need not
equal the magnetic-axis major radius.

The [radial outline of the plasma
boundary](name:radial_outline_of_plasma_boundary) instead specifies
major-radius coordinates along the boundary contour. Within the same
coordinate family, the [radial coordinate of a conductor
cross-section](name:radial_coordinate_of_conductor_cross_section) locates a
device reference position rather than this plasma reference position.

The axis defined solely by the geometry of the relevant object or plasma
cross-section. Where $R_{\mathrm{geo}} = (R_{\max} + R_{\min})/2,\quad
Z_{\mathrm{geo}} = (Z_{\max} + Z_{\min})/2$, $R_{\max}, R_{\min}$ is the
radial extrema of the cross-section; $Z_{\max}, Z_{\min}$ is its vertical
extrema.

items.name: parallel_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity
items.description:
Parallel current density due to heat viscosity is the signed charge flux
along the local magnetic field generated by heat-viscosity stresses in a
collisional magnetized plasma.
items.documentation:
Parallel current density due to heat viscosity is the magnetic-field-aligned
component of the electric-current contribution generated by heat-viscosity
stresses in a collisional magnetized-plasma fluid closure.

Its defining projection is

$$
j_\parallel = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $j_\parallel$ is the parallel current density due to heat viscosity,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}$ is the [heat-viscosity current-density
vector](name:current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$
is the unit vector along the local magnetic field. Specifically,
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, where $\mathbf{B}$ is the
magnetic-field vector and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude; the projection
requires a nonzero magnetic field.

This is a local, unaveraged contribution to [electric current
density](name:current_density), not a surface-integrated current or the
total current density from all mechanisms. It represents net plasma charge
transport attributable to heat viscosity, rather than an individual species
contribution; the definition imposes no restriction to a particular plasma
region.

Unlike [toroidal current density due to heat
viscosity](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), which
projects the same parent vector onto the geometric toroidal direction, this
quantity projects along the local magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when the heat-viscosity conventional electric
current flows along the local magnetic-field vector.

items.name: voltage_of_mass_spectrometer_channel
items.description:
Signed bias potential applied between the photomultiplier detector electrode
and its electronics reference for one mass-resolved channel, setting
ion-signal gain.
items.documentation:
The mass-spectrometer channel voltage is the detector-bias potential
difference associated with one channel assigned to a selected atomic mass.
It is an instrumental operating parameter of the photomultiplier detector
that controls the gain applied to the collected ion signal, rather than a
plasma thermodynamic or field quantity.

The defining potential difference is

$$
V_{\mathrm{ch}} = \phi_{\mathrm{det}} - \phi_{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is the channel detector-bias voltage,
$\phi_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the electric potential of the photomultiplier
detector electrode, and $\phi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the electronics reference
potential.

This quantity applies to one mass-resolved channel and its associated
detector circuit. It is not summed or averaged across channels, mass
assignments, detector electrodes, or ion populations, and it does not
represent a local plasma voltage.

The channel-level quantity specializes the device-level [mass-spectrometer
detector bias voltage](name:voltage_of_mass_spectrometer) to one channel. It
is distinct from the [ion current of a mass-spectrometer
channel](name:ion_current_of_mass_spectrometer_channel), which is the
collected electrical signal, and from the [voltage of a spectrometer
channel](name:voltage_of_spectrometer_channel), which denotes an electrical
output signal rather than the detector-bias potential.

Sign convention: Positive when the detector electrode potential exceeds the
electronics reference potential.

items.name: ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Signed local volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional energy exchange for ions
in a specified charge state, positive for net energy gain and negative for
net energy loss.
items.documentation:
Ion charge-state collisional power density is the net local volumetric
energy exchange caused by Coulomb collisions for ions in a specified charge
state. It includes the contributing thermal and fast ion populations
represented by that charge state.

$$
P_{i,z}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_b Q_{i,z\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_{i,z}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional power density for ion
population $i$ in charge state $z$, and $Q_{i,z\leftarrow
b}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the rate of collisional energy transfer from partner
population $b$ to that target. The sum covers the collision partners
included by the aggregation scope. This is the charge-state-resolved
specialization of [power density due to
collisions](name:power_density_due_to_collisions); unlike [fast-ion
charge-state collisional power
density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions), it is
not restricted to fast ions.

Sign convention: Positive when the specified ion charge state gains energy
from its collision partners.

items.name: neutral_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective vector velocity at which neutral particle momentum is advectively
transported in edge-plasma fluid models, aggregated over all neutral species
and excited states as a transport closure coefficient distinct from the
actual neutral particle flow velocity.
items.documentation:
The neutral momentum convection velocity is the effective bulk vector
velocity appearing in the non-diffusive, advective contribution to neutral
momentum transport in edge-plasma and scrape-off-layer fluid models. It
encapsulates the net effect of charge-exchange, ionization, and
recombination reactions on the aggregate neutral momentum balance across all
neutral species and excited states, serving as a transport closure
coefficient rather than the physical flow speed of any individual neutral
population.

In multi-fluid edge-plasma transport frameworks, the total neutral momentum
flux is decomposed into a diffusive part proportional to the local
momentum-density gradient and a convective (pinch-like) part proportional to
the momentum density:

$$
\mathbf{F}_p = -D_p \nabla p_n + \mathbf{V}_c \, p_n
$$

where $D_p$ is the neutral momentum diffusivity and $p_n$ is the neutral
momentum density. The convection velocity $\mathbf{V}_c$ (this quantity)
drives advective momentum transport independently of the local gradient,
functioning as a neutral momentum pinch.

The quantity is computed in fluid neutral transport solvers as a closure
derived from atomic physics rate coefficients and the local plasma state.
Its directional projections include the
radial_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity ($R$ component) and the
vertical_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity ($Z$ component) in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The analogous
charge-state-resolved quantity is
[radial_neutral_state_effective_momentum_convection_velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity).
The parent momentum_convection_velocity establishes the general
momentum-flux decomposition framework from which this neutral-species
specialization is derived.

items.name: lower_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Dimensionless Luce shape coefficient measuring how the lower outboard
(low-field-side) corner of the plasma boundary departs from the reference
ellipse defined by boundary minor radius, lower elongation, and lower
triangularity.
items.documentation:
The lower outer squareness $\zeta_{lo}$ is one of four corner-specific shape
parameters in the Luce (2013) plasma boundary parameterization, describing
how much the lower outer quadrant of the plasma cross-section boundary
deviates from the reference ellipse defined by the boundary minor radius
$a$, lower elongation $\kappa_l$, and lower triangularity $\delta_l$. The
lower outer quadrant is the low-field-side, large-$R$ corner below the
magnetic-axis height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

Within the Luce corner parameterization, the coefficient is related to the
lower-outer superellipse exponent $n_{lo}$ by

$$
\zeta_{lo} = 1 - \frac{2}{n_{lo}}
$$

where $n_{lo}$ controls the local corner curvature of the lower-outboard
boundary segment. The reference ellipse corresponds to $n_{lo}=2$.

Positive values indicate that the lower-outboard boundary corner lies
outside the reference ellipse at the corresponding corner location, giving a
more rectangular boundary; $\zeta_{lo}=0$ indicates the reference ellipse;
negative values indicate that the corner lies inside the reference ellipse,
giving inward concavity relative to that ellipse. This coefficient excludes
the upper-outboard and high-field-side corner contributions represented by
[upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary),
[lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary),
and
[upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary);
[outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary)
combines the outboard corner behavior, and
[squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:squareness_of_plasma_boundary) is the
global single-coefficient summary.

items.name: normalized_ion_species_number_density
items.description:
Normalized ion-species number density is the particle-density perturbation
of one ion species in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, scaled by a positive
reference density.
items.documentation:
Normalized ion-species number density is the normalized zeroth
velocity-space moment of the perturbed particle distribution for one
selected ion species in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. Its moment weighting
counts particles rather than weighting them by charge, mass, or energy.

The normalized density perturbation is defined by:

$$
\widehat{n}_s = \frac{\widetilde{n}_s}{n_{\mathrm{ref}}} = \frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{ref}}}\int \widetilde{f}^{\,p}_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\widehat{n}_s$ is the normalized density perturbation,
$\widetilde{n}_s$ is the particle-number-density perturbation, $s$ labels
the ion species, and $n_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference density.
The function $\widetilde{f}^{\,p}_s$ is the perturbed particle distribution,
with superscript $p$ identifying particle rather than gyrocenter variables;
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element. The integral covers all velocity space.

The species contribution is summed over all ionic charge states, with no
summation over different ion species and no thermal-only restriction. It is
local rather than a flux-surface or volume average. It represents a
perturbation, not the equilibrium species-to-reference density ratio. Any
eigenmode phase is retained: neither a modulus nor a squared fluctuation is
implied. The particular reference density and the eigenmode amplitude
convention are not fixed by this quantity.

Unlike [normalized gyrocenter perturbed
density](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_density), this moment uses the
particle distribution, including the transformation from gyrocenter to
particle variables. It is therefore distinct from an explicitly
[first-order-Bessel-weighted gyrocenter density
moment](name:normalized_perturbed_gyrocenter_density_bessel_1).

items.name: poloidal_current_weighted_average_external_magnetic_flux
items.description:
Poloidal magnetic flux from all external active coils and passive loops is
averaged over the plasma cross-section with toroidal-current-density
weighting, excluding plasma-generated flux.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic flux averaged with toroidal plasma current density
represents the externally generated flux linked by the distributed plasma
current. It is the poloidal specialization of [current-weighted average
external magnetic
flux](name:current_weighted_average_external_magnetic_flux), and an
averaged, source-separated form of [magnetic flux](name:magnetic_flux).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when viewed
from above, and $Z$ is vertical height, the average is defined by

$$
\overline{\Phi}_{\mathrm{p,ext}} = \frac{1}{I_{\mathrm{p}}}\int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{p}}}\Phi_{\mathrm{p,ext}}(R,Z)\,j_\phi(R,Z)\,dA_{RZ}
$$

where $\overline{\Phi}_{\mathrm{p,ext}}$ is the current-weighted average
external poloidal magnetic flux, $\Omega_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the plasma
poloidal cross-section, $j_\phi$ is the toroidal plasma current density, and
$dA_{RZ}$ is the poloidal cross-sectional area element. The normalization is
the signed [plasma current](name:plasma_current),
$I_{\mathrm{p}}=\int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{p}}}j_\phi\,dA_{RZ}$. The local
external contribution $\Phi_{\mathrm{p,ext}}$ follows the [poloidal magnetic
flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) definition: flux through a horizontal
disk centered on the toroidal symmetry axis and bounded by the toroidal
circle through the evaluation point.

The external contribution includes all active coils and passive conducting
loops, including induced currents in conducting structures, but excludes
flux generated by the plasma current itself. The weighting uses signed
toroidal plasma current density, not its absolute value; consequently, this
quantity is distinct from an unweighted area average. The definition
requires nonzero total plasma current.

Sign convention: Positive when the external disk flux, averaged with the
signed weights $j_\phi/I_{\mathrm{p}}$, threads the horizontal disks in the
$+Z$ direction.

items.name: volume_averaged_neutral_temperature
items.description:
Volume-averaged neutral temperature is the translational kinetic
temperature, expressed as energy per particle, of a neutral population
throughout the plasma volume inside the last closed magnetic flux surface
during plasma initiation.
items.documentation:
Volume-averaged neutral temperature is the translational kinetic temperature
of a neutral population during plasma initiation, representing random
translational energy after removal of mean flow. It excludes energy stored
in internal excitation or other internal quantum states.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_{n} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}}\int_{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} T_n(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\overline{T}_{n}$ is the volume-averaged neutral temperature,
$T_n(\mathbf{x})$ is the local translational kinetic temperature of the
neutral population at position $\mathbf{x}$, $V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the
plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface, and
$\mathrm{d}V$ is the differential physical-volume element.

The quantity applies to the represented neutral population throughout the
volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface during plasma
initiation. Its aggregation convention is an arithmetic spatial volume
average of the local temperature, not a local value or a density-weighted
particle average. It does not select only the cold or energetic neutral
component and is not restricted to a particular internal quantum state.

This quantity is obtained by applying the volume-averaging transformation to
[neutral temperature](name:neutral_temperature), with the local population
and state aggregation inherited from that quantity. [Cold neutral
temperature](name:cold_neutral_temperature) and [hot neutral
temperature](name:hot_neutral_temperature_at_plasma_boundary) are
population-restricted alternatives, while [neutral internal state
temperature](name:neutral_internal_state_temperature) resolves a specified
internal state rather than the generic neutral population.

items.name: outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Dimensionless Luce shape coefficient measuring how both outboard
(low-field-side) corners of the plasma boundary depart from the reference
ellipse defined by minor radius, elongation, and triangularity.
items.documentation:
The outer squareness of the plasma boundary is the Luce (2013) dimensionless
shape coefficient characterizing how the low-field-side (large-$R$) corners
of the last-closed flux surface poloidal cross-section depart from the
reference ellipse defined by the boundary minor radius $a$, elongation
$\kappa$, and triangularity $\delta$. It is the parent quantity for
[upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary)
and
[lower_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:lower_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary),
which resolve the upper-outboard and lower-outboard corner contributions
separately.

A positive outer squareness indicates the outboard corners of the plasma
cross-section lie outside the reference ellipse (a more rectangular
boundary), while a negative value indicates inward concavity at the outboard
corners. The outer squareness is particularly sensitive to X-point geometry
and the configuration of low-field-side shaping coils, making it relevant to
heat-load distribution and edge stability.

Outer squareness is inferred from equilibrium reconstruction by fitting the
poloidal boundary contour $\{R(\xi), Z(\xi)\}$, where $\xi$ is a poloidal
parameter, to external magnetic measurements and internal constraints. The
global single-coefficient summary is provided by
[squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:squareness_of_plasma_boundary), while
the high-field-side corner contributions are captured by
[lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary)
and upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary.

items.name: z_direction_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector
items.description:
Z component of the unit vector aligned with the unshattered pellet velocity
immediately before shattering, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y,
z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the signed projection of the unshattered pellet-injection
direction onto the Cartesian z axis immediately before shattering. It
describes orientation only, not the pellet speed or the velocity of
shattered fragments.

The component is defined by:

$$
d_z = \hat{\mathbf{d}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{d}}$ is the unit vector aligned with the unshattered
pellet velocity and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along increasing z
in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame. Together
with the corresponding [x component](name:x_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector)
and [y component](name:y_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector), it specifies the
injection direction.

items.name: ammonia_source_rate
items.description:
Instantaneous ammonia source rate expressed as equivalent-electron count per
time, assigning ten count units to each neutral NH3 molecule introduced into
the plasma vessel.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the instantaneous rate of ammonia delivery to the plasma
vessel, expressed using the equivalent-electron convention for neutral
ammonia molecules. It represents injected NH3 inventory, not the plasma
electron source or the ionization state of ammonia.

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}} = 10\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{NH_3}}
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{NH_3}}$ is the molecular ammonia injection rate, and the
factor 10 is the total atomic-electron count of one neutral NH3 molecule.
Time integration gives the corresponding
[accumulated_ammonia_count](name:accumulated_ammonia_count). The
isotopologue-specific counterpart is
[ammonia_deuterated_source_rate](name:ammonia_deuterated_source_rate).

items.name: tungsten_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Particle number density of the tungsten ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local tungsten-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all positive ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of the tungsten ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local tungsten-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all positive ionic charge states. It represents
tungsten ions specifically, rather than electrons, other ion species, or
neutral tungsten.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
n_{W,\mathrm{axis}} = \sum_{q=1}^{q_{\max}} n_{W^{q+},\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{W,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the tungsten ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $W$ denotes tungsten, $q$ is the positive integer ionic
charge state, $q_{\max}$ is the highest included tungsten charge state, and
$n_{W^{q+},\mathrm{axis}}$ is the number density of tungsten ions in charge
state $q$ at the magnetic axis.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete positively charged tungsten-ion
population at that location, summed over charge states; it is neither a
flux-surface or volume integral nor the density of neutral tungsten or one
individual charge state.

This is the tungsten-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It differs
from [xenon density at the magnetic
axis](name:xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis), which applies the same local,
charge-state-summed convention to xenon ions instead of tungsten ions.

items.name: parallel_runaway_electron_current_density
items.description:
Parallel runaway-electron current density is the signed field-aligned
component of conventional current density carried by runaway electrons.
items.documentation:
Parallel runaway-electron current density is the signed field-aligned
contribution to conventional electric-current density carried by runaway
electrons. It is the runaway-electron contribution to [parallel current
density](name:parallel_current_density), not the total plasma current.

For a flux-surface-resolved value, the magnetic-field-weighted definition
is:

$$
j_{\parallel,\mathrm{RE}}^{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{\left\langle \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}\cdot\mathbf{B}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}}{B_0}
$$

where $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{RE}}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the flux-surface-resolved
parallel runaway-electron current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the
current-density vector carried by runaway electrons, $\mathbf{B}$ is the
magnetic-field vector, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes a
flux-surface average, and $B_0$ is the signed reference vacuum toroidal
magnetic field. The reference field is positive toward increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$
is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The contribution includes runaway electrons without restriction to a
particular orbit class; currents carried by other particle populations are
excluded. It is a signed scalar component, not the magnitude of the
runaway-electron current-density vector, a toroidal projection, or total
[current density](name:current_density).

At a point, the field-aligned component is the projection of the
current-density vector onto the local magnetic-field direction,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, where
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the local magnetic-field unit
vector and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is the magnetic-field magnitude. The flux-surface
value above is not generally the unweighted flux-surface average of this
pointwise component. [Volume-averaged parallel runaway-electron current
density](name:volume_averaged_parallel_runaway_electron_current_density)
instead uses a plasma-volume average.

Sign convention: Positive when the flux-surface-averaged contraction
$\langle\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{RE}}\cdot\mathbf{B}\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ has
the same sign as $B_0, with $B_0$ positive toward increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: difference_of_fast_neutral_beam_motional_stark_wavelength_and_fast_neutral_beam_reference_wavelength_of_spectral_line
items.description:
Signed wavelength displacement of a selected fast-neutral-beam spectral-line
component from its reference wavelength, caused by the motional Stark
electric field.
items.documentation:
The motional-Stark wavelength displacement is the signed separation between
a selected spectral-line component from fast neutral beam particles and its
unshifted reference wavelength. It represents the Lorentz shift produced by
the electric field arising from particle motion across the magnetic field.

$$
\Delta\lambda_{\mathrm{MS}} = \lambda_{\mathrm{component}} - \lambda_{\mathrm{reference}}
$$

where $\Delta\lambda_{\mathrm{MS}}$ is the motional-Stark wavelength
displacement, $\lambda_{\mathrm{component}}$ is the wavelength of the
selected component, and $\lambda_{\mathrm{reference}}$ is the corresponding
unshifted wavelength. The motional electric field is
$\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{motional}} = \mathbf{v} \times \mathbf{B}$, where
$\mathbf{v}$ is the fast-neutral velocity and $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic
field.

This quantity is distinct from the Doppler wavelength difference caused by
line-of-sight motion, represented by [difference of neutral-beam Doppler
wavelength and neutral-beam reference
wavelength](name:difference_of_neutral_beam_doppler_wavelength_and_reference_wavelength_of_spectral_line).
Positive displacement denotes a component at a longer wavelength than the
reference.

items.name: exposure_time_of_spectrometer_channel
items.description:
Temporal duration over which a spectrometer channel accumulates incident
photons to form one spectral measurement.
items.documentation:
The integration duration is the elapsed time between the start and end of
the photon-accumulation interval for a spectrometer channel. It defines the
temporal window contributing to one spectral measurement and is distinct
from the channel's spectral response, including its [effective spectral
width](name:effective_spectral_width_of_spectrometer_channel).

It is defined by

$$
\Delta t = t_{\mathrm{end}} - t_{\mathrm{start}}
$$

where $\Delta t$ is the integration duration, and $t_{\mathrm{start}}$ and
$t_{\mathrm{end}}$ are the times at which photon accumulation begins and
ends. The accumulated signal is determined by the time integral of the
incident spectral flux over this interval.

items.name: neutral_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
items.description:
Incident neutral energy flux per unit plasma-facing wall area carried by
neutral particles associated with recombination at the surface, summed over
incident-ion species, incident-ion charge states, recombination channels,
neutral species, and internal states.
items.documentation:
Neutral energy flux at the wall due to recombination quantifies the rate at
which recombination-associated energy carried by neutral particles is
incident on a plasma-facing surface per unit area. It is the
neutral-particle carrier of energy associated with recombination or
neutralization processes at the boundary, not the outgoing neutral emission
from the surface.

The incident neutral recombination energy flux at wall location
$\mathbf{x}_w$ is defined as the energy moment of the incident neutral
particle-flux distribution:

$$
Q_{\mathrm{rec},n}^{\mathrm{inc}}(\mathbf{x}_w) = \sum_{i,\,\zeta,\,c,\,a,\,k}\int E_\mathrm{in}\,\frac{d\Gamma^{\mathrm{inc}}_{i,\zeta,c,a,k}}{dE_\mathrm{in}}(\mathbf{x}_w,E_\mathrm{in})\,dE_\mathrm{in}
$$

where $Q_{\mathrm{rec},n}^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident neutral energy
flux at the wall due to recombination, $\mathbf{x}_w$ is a wall-surface
location, the subscript $n$ denotes the neutral-particle channel, the
superscript $\mathrm{inc}$ denotes the incident wall-crossing direction, $i$
identifies the incident-ion species, $\zeta$ the incident-ion charge state,
$c$ the surface recombination or neutralization channel, $a$ the neutral
species, $k$ the neutral internal state, $E_\mathrm{in}$ the energy carried
by a neutral particle crossing the surface in the incident direction, and
$d\Gamma^{\mathrm{inc}}_{i,\zeta,c,a,k}/dE_\mathrm{in}$ the corresponding
incident neutral particle-flux distribution with respect to $E_\mathrm{in}$.
For discrete incident-neutral energies, the integral is replaced by the
corresponding sum.

This quantity applies to neutral particles crossing the plasma-facing
surface toward the material. It is aggregated over incident-ion species,
incident-ion charge states, recombination or neutralization channels,
neutral species, and neutral internal states; no neutral species, state,
incident-ion species, or charge-state resolution remains. It excludes
ion-carried energy flux, photon or radiation energy flux, outgoing neutral
recombination products, and the subsequent partition of incident energy into
wall heating, reflection, or re-emission.

This quantity is the energy-weighted counterpart of [incident neutral
particle flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination),
which counts the same incident neutral population without weighting by
$E_\mathrm{in}$. It is directionally distinct from [neutral particle flux at
the wall due to
recombination](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination),
which refers to outgoing neutral recombination products, and it is not the
total [energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination). [Ion energy
flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) describes
the ion-associated channel rather than neutral-carried incident energy.

Sign convention: Positive when neutral particles carrying
recombination-associated energy cross the plasma-facing surface from the
plasma-facing volume toward the material surface.

items.name: toroidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe
items.description:
The toroidal angle of a toroidal magnetic-field probe is the signed
azimuthal orientation of the probe sensitive-axis normal projected onto the
horizontal plane, measured from +R toward increasing φ in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. Opposite projected normals are folded into the
same principal orientation.
items.documentation:
The toroidal angle of a toroidal magnetic-field probe is the signed
azimuthal orientation of the probe sensitive-axis normal after projection
onto the horizontal plane spanned by $\hat R$ and $\hat\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Its zero direction is
the outward radial direction, and the projected normal is treated as an
orientation axis rather than a directed vector.

The angle is defined by the two-argument arctangent of the horizontal normal
components, folded modulo $\pi$ into the principal interval $(-\pi/2,
\pi/2]$:

$$
\alpha_\phi = \mathcal{F}_{(-\pi/2,\pi/2]}\!\left(\operatorname{atan2}(n_\phi,n_R)\right)
$$

where $\alpha_\phi$ is this toroidal angle, $n_R$ and $n_\phi$ are the
radial and toroidal scalar components of the normalized probe sensitive-axis
normal vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and
$\mathcal{F}_{(-\pi/2,\pi/2]}(\beta)$ denotes the representative of an angle
$\beta$ after adding an integer multiple of $\pi$ that lies in $(-\pi/2,
\pi/2]$.

This quantity applies only to toroidal magnetic-field probes and is defined
separately for each probe. It describes sensor orientation, not the
[toroidal angle](name:toroidal_angle) that locates a point and not the probe
position; no aggregation over multiple probes is implied.

With the modulo-$\pi$ folding, projections parallel or antiparallel to
$+\hat R$ have $\alpha_\phi=0$, and projections parallel or antiparallel to
$+\hat\phi$ have the principal value $\alpha_\phi=\pi/2$. Together with the
[poloidal angle of a toroidal magnetic-field
probe](name:poloidal_angle_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), it specifies
the orientation of the same sensitive-axis normal; it is the
toroidal-field-probe-specific counterpart of the [toroidal angle of a
magnetic-field probe](name:toroidal_angle_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe).

Sign convention: Positive when the horizontal orientation is tilted from the
radial basis line toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: absorbed_radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module
items.description:
Net photon power retained by a breeding blanket module after reflection of
incident plasma radiation at its plasma-facing surface.
items.documentation:
The absorbed radiated power of a breeding blanket module is the net
electromagnetic photon power retained by the module after plasma radiation
interacts with its plasma-facing surface. It includes absorbed
bremsstrahlung and atomic line radiation and is the absorbed component of
the broader [radiated power of a breeder blanket
module](name:radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module).

The absorbed power is related to the [incident radiated power of a breeder
blanket module](name:incident_radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module) by:

$$
P_\text{abs} = (1 - \mathcal{R}) P_\text{inc}
$$

where $P_\text{inc}$ is the incident radiative power, $\mathcal{R}$ is the
effective hemispherical surface reflectance averaged over the incident
photon spectrum, and $P_\text{abs}$ is the absorbed radiated power. This
quantity excludes photon power reflected from the surface and nuclear energy
deposited within the module.

items.name: toroidal_trapped_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Toroidal component of the Coulomb-collisional torque density transferred to
trapped fast ions, measuring angular-momentum transfer about the symmetry
axis.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the toroidal projection of the angular-momentum transfer
rate per unit plasma volume delivered to trapped fast ions by Coulomb
collisions with background plasma species. It resolves the parent trapped
fast-ion collisional torque density specifically about the toroidal symmetry
axis.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional torque-density
vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, and
$\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its scalar component. The vectors are
expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$
frame, with $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ and
$\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}$ represented in N.m$^{-2}$.

Only the trapped fast-ion population and Coulomb-collision contribution are
included; other orbit classes, ion populations, and collision-independent
torque sources are excluded.

Sign convention: Positive when the collisional angular-momentum transfer to
trapped fast ions points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$.

items.name: trapped_fast_particle_density
items.description:
Trapped fast-particle density is the number density of nonthermal particles
of a selected species on magnetically trapped guiding-center orbits, whose
parallel motion reverses at magnetic mirror points. It may be specified
locally or averaged over a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Trapped fast-particle density is the number density of nonthermal particles
of a selected species on magnetically trapped guiding-center orbits. These
orbits reverse their motion parallel to the magnetic field at mirror points.

At position $\mathbf{x}$, the local density is the zeroth velocity-space
moment of the fast-particle distribution restricted to trapped orbits:

$$
n_s(\mathbf{x}) = \int_{\mathcal{V}_{s,\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x})} f_s^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_s$ is the trapped fast-particle density of species $s$, $s$ labels
the selected species, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $f_s^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle velocity distribution
of species $s$, $\mathcal{V}_{s,\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the
velocity-space region for trapped guiding-center orbits at $\mathbf{x}$, and
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The quantity applies to nonthermal particles of one selected species,
without implicitly combining different species. It may be expressed as a
local density, which can vary over a magnetic flux surface, or as the
average of that local density over the surface.

Thermal particles and fast particles on passing orbits are excluded. In
particular, co-passing and counter-passing fast-particle populations are
distinct from the trapped population.

This is the trapped-orbit contribution to [fast-particle
density](name:fast_particle_density); [co-passing fast-particle
density](name:co_passing_fast_particle_density) and [counter-passing
fast-particle density](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_density) describe
distinct passing orbit classes. It is the nonthermal component of [total
trapped-particle density](name:total_trapped_particle_density), which also
includes thermal particles.

items.name: resistivity_of_plasma_facing_component
items.description:
Electrical resistivity of the material assigned to a mobile plasma-facing
component unit, relating local electric field to current density and
governing its conductive electromagnetic response.
items.documentation:
Electrical resistivity is the material property that determines the electric
field required to sustain conduction in a mobile plasma-facing component
unit. It governs induced-current and eddy-current response within that unit.

For an isotropic material, the local constitutive relation is

$$
\mathbf{E} = \rho\,\mathbf{J}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric-field vector, $\rho$ is the
electrical resistivity, and $\mathbf{J}$ is the conventional current-density
vector.

This quantity applies to the material of one mobile plasma-facing component
unit and is not summed over multiple units or converted into a lumped
resistance. It is a local material property, distinct from the effective
resistivity of a broader passive conducting structure or [wall
material](name:resistivity_of_wall_material). When geometry is included, it
contributes to a lumped [passive-loop
resistance](name:resistance_of_passive_loop), which also depends on
current-path length and cross-sectional geometry.

items.name: toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Toroidal flux-limiter coefficient that sets an edge-region, nonnegative cap
on the toroidal component of neutral-particle momentum-flux density for a
specified internal state as a fraction of its collisionless free-streaming
bound, without reversing the signed component.
items.documentation:
Toroidal flux-limiter coefficient that applies to neutral particles
occupying a specified internal state over the edge region is the directional
coefficient used to bound the toroidal component of the corresponding
neutral internal-state momentum-flux density. The internal state may be an
electronic, vibrational, rotational, or other resolved excitation state, and
the toroidal component is the projection along $\hat{\phi}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R},
\hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle
increasing counterclockwise when viewed from $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

For the toroidal direction, the limiter defines the admissible cap:

$$
|\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},\phi}| \le \alpha_{\phi}\,|\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},\phi}|,\qquad 0 \le \alpha_{\phi} \le 1
$$

where $\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},\phi}$ is the limited toroidal component of the
neutral internal-state momentum flux over the edge region,
$\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},\phi}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming
toroidal component whose magnitude defines the bound, and $\alpha_{\phi}$ is
this toroidal limiter coefficient.

The inequality is a cap on magnitude rather than an equality for the
realized momentum flux. Because $\alpha_{\phi}$ is nonnegative, applying the
limiter may reduce or bound a signed toroidal momentum-flux component but
does not reverse its direction; a nonzero limited component retains the sign
of the underlying toroidal component. This scalar coefficient is the
toroidal member of the [neutral internal-state momentum-flux limiter
coefficient over the edge
region](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region),
is distinct from the [toroidal neutral internal-state momentum
flux](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux), and is in the
same directional family as the [parallel neutral internal-state
momentum-flux limiter
coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
and the [poloidal momentum neutral internal-state flux-limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_momentum_neutral_internal_state_flux_limiter_coefficient).

items.name: neutral_state_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective velocity multiplying the number density of neutral particles in a
specified internal state to give their convective particle flux.
items.documentation:
Neutral-state convection velocity is the effective vector coefficient of the
density-proportional advective particle flux for one resolved internal state
of a neutral species. It describes directed particle transport after
density-gradient-driven diffusion has been separated.

The convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s}^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_s\mathbf{v}_{s}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $s$ identifies the specified internal state of the neutral species,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is its convective particle flux,
$n_s$ is its particle number density, and $\mathbf{v}_{s}^{\mathrm{conv}}$
is this effective convection velocity.

The coefficient applies to the particle-number balance of that species and
state, including both thermal and nonthermal particles. It is not summed or
averaged over internal states or neutral species. The vector definition has
no prescribed directional projection; for transport across magnetic flux
surfaces, its outward-normal projection distinguishes outward convection
from inward pinch.

The quantity excludes density-gradient-driven diffusive transport and does
not represent a heat- or momentum-transport coefficient. It need not equal
the [bulk neutral internal-state
velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity), which is the first
velocity moment of the state's particle distribution.

When internal states of the same species are combined, their convective
particle fluxes add. Consequently, the corresponding [effective
neutral-particle convection
velocity](name:effective_neutral_particle_convection_velocity) is the
number-density-weighted mean of the state-resolved coefficients, not their
sum.

Sign convention: Positive when the flux-surface-normal convective transport
is outward toward the last closed flux surface; negative when it is inward
toward the magnetic axis.

items.name: vertical_angular_width_of_camera
items.description:
Angular extent of a camera’s imaging coverage along the vertical Z direction
of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical angular width is the total angular span covered by a camera’s
imaging region in the detector plane along the physical vertical direction.
It is a non-negative field-of-view quantity, independent of the signs of the
individual viewing angles.

The width is defined by the difference between the largest and smallest
covered vertical viewing angles:

$$
\Delta\theta_{\mathrm{vert}} = \theta_{\mathrm{vert,max}} - \theta_{\mathrm{vert,min}}
$$

where $\Delta\theta_{\mathrm{vert}}$ is the vertical angular width and
$\theta_{\mathrm{vert,max}}$ and $\theta_{\mathrm{vert,min}}$ are the upper
and lower signed vertical viewing-angle limits, expressed in radians. The
vertical direction is $+Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

This full-span quantity is distinct from the signed [vertical angle of a
detector pixel](name:vertical_angle_of_detector_pixel). Its directional
counterpart is the [toroidal angular width of a
camera](name:toroidal_angular_width_of_camera).

items.name: parallel_net_ion_momentum_source
items.description:
Area-normalized net rate of ion momentum transfer along the local magnetic
field, summed algebraically over ionic charge states and contributing source
and sink processes.
items.documentation:
The parallel net ion momentum source is the signed, area-normalized rate of
[momentum](name:momentum) transfer to the ion population along the local
magnetic field. It is the field-aligned projection of the vector [net ion
momentum source](name:net_ion_momentum_source), not its magnitude.

The projection and aggregation are defined by

$$
S_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{net}} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf S_i^{\mathrm{net}} = \sum_q\sum_a \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf S_{iq}^{(a)}
$$

where $S_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{net}}$ is this parallel source, $\mathbf
S_i^{\mathrm{net}}$ is the net ion momentum-source vector, and $\mathbf
S_{iq}^{(a)}$ is the area-normalized momentum-source contribution from
process $a$ to ionic charge state $q$ of ion population $i$. The unit vector
$\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ points along the nonzero local
magnetic field $\mathbf B$.

All ionic charge states and contributing source and sink processes are
summed algebraically, allowing opposing contributions to cancel. The
quantity is charge-state summed rather than charge-state resolved;
momentum-source terms assigned to electrons or neutrals are excluded. Its
area normalization does not make it a [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux):
it describes momentum supplied to or removed from ions, rather than momentum
transported across a surface.

Sign convention: Positive when the net transfer of ion momentum is in the
direction of the local magnetic field.

items.name: heat_convection_velocity
items.description:
Heat convection velocity is the effective advective velocity whose product
with thermal-energy density gives the convective heat flux. It characterizes
heat transport only and does not imply equality to any bulk fluid velocity.
items.documentation:
Heat convection velocity is the effective advective velocity associated with
