convective transport of thermal energy. It relates a convective heat-flux
component to the corresponding thermal-energy density for the same heat
population, without requiring the effective velocity to equal a bulk fluid
velocity.

For a scalar component along an oriented transport direction, the defining
relation is

$$
q_h^{\mathrm{conv}} = w_h v_h^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $q_h^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective heat-flux component, $w_h$ is
the thermal-energy density of the transported heat population, and
$v_h^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the heat convection velocity.

This quantity is heat-specific: it is not a generic convection velocity for
arbitrary plasma scalars. For species-level specializations such as [ion
heat convection velocity](name:ion_heat_convection_velocity), the effective
velocity is an intensive quantity and is the density-weighted mean over all
charge states of the species.

Sign convention: Positive when the associated convective heat-flux component
is directed along the positive orientation of the transport direction used
for that component.

items.name: total_fast_particle_count
items.description:
Volume-integrated number of suprathermal particles, combining all included
fast-particle species and superposed fast-particle distributions.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the total number of nonthermal or suprathermal particles
represented by the included fast-particle distributions over the plasma
volume. It is an extensive particle-count measure, not a local density or a
count of numerical distribution markers.

$$
N_{\mathrm{fast}} = \int_V n_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{r})\,d^3\mathbf{r}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the total fast-particle count, $V$ is the
plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $n_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the
[fast-particle density](name:fast_particle_density) summed over the included
fast-particle species and superposed distributions. The count excludes
particles belonging only to the thermal population and is related to the
volume-integrated [fast-particle energy](name:fast_particle_energy), which
weights the same population by kinetic energy.

items.name: volume_of_ferritic_element
items.description:
Geometric volume enclosed by the boundaries of a ferritic in-vessel element,
representing its complete material extent rather than a cross-sectional
dimension.
items.documentation:
The volume of a ferritic in-vessel element is the non-negative geometric
measure of the material region bounded by the element’s physical boundary.
It represents the element as a whole, rather than a single cross-sectional
dimension such as its [ferritic-element
width](name:width_of_ferritic_element).

The volume is defined by

$$
V = \int_{\Omega} d^3x
$$

where $V$ is the element volume, $\Omega$ is the region occupied by the
ferritic element, and $d^3x$ is the differential volume element. The
quantity excludes surrounding plasma, vacuum, and unrelated neighboring
structures.

items.name: electron_number_density
items.description:
Free-electron column abundance associated with an electromagnetic
propagation path, before a narrower line, chord, or complete-path qualifier
is fixed. It counts unbound electrons accumulated by a path integral, not a
local volume density or a path-averaged density.
items.documentation:
Electron number density for electromagnetic-wave propagation is the
path-accumulated abundance of free electrons associated with a specified
propagation path. It represents unbound-electron population in a column
along that path, rather than a charge-weighted, mass-weighted, or
energy-weighted density.

For an electromagnetic propagation path $\mathcal{C}$, the parent column
quantity is defined by

$$
N_e[\mathcal{C}] = \int_{\mathcal{C}} n_e(\mathbf{r}(l))\,dl
$$

where $N_e[\mathcal{C}]$ is the electron number density as a path-column
quantity, $\mathcal{C}$ is the propagation path or path portion specified by
the more specific quantity, $n_e(\mathbf{r}(l))$ is the local [free-electron
number density](name:electron_density) at position $\mathbf{r}(l)$,
$\mathbf{r}(l)$ is position along the path, $l$ is path distance, and $dl$
is the differential path length.

The scope is free electrons accumulated along an electromagnetic propagation
path. The aggregation convention at this parent level is path-column
accumulation; the parent does not itself fix a complete-path, one-way,
return-path, chord-specific, or normalized convention. Bound electrons,
ions, neutral particles, local volume density, path-averaged density, volume
integrals, and charge-weighted densities are excluded.

The [line-integrated electron number
density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density) specializes this
parent by fixing a line-integration path convention. The parent supplies the
free-electron population and column-accumulation semantics, while the child
supplies the additional path qualifier. The [line-averaged electron
density](name:line_averaged_electron_density) is the corresponding path
average and is obtained only after dividing the column quantity by the total
path length for the same chosen path.

items.name: deuterium_tritium_density
items.description:
Deuterium-tritium density is the local ion number density of the
deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species, treating deuterium and tritium as
one effective species.
items.documentation:
Deuterium-tritium density is the local ion number density of the
deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species, treating deuterium and tritium
ions as one effective species. It is a species-level per-volume particle
count summed over all ion charge states.

The defining relation is the sum of the component fuel-ion number densities:

$$
n_{DT} = n_D + n_T
$$

where $n_{DT}$ is the deuterium-tritium density, $n_D$ is the [deuterium
density](name:deuterium_density), and $n_T$ is the [tritium
density](name:tritium_density). Each component density is
charge-state-summed over the corresponding ion charge states; the
dimensionless tritium fraction, where used, is $f_T = n_T/n_{DT}$.

This quantity includes only deuterium and tritium fuel ions represented by
the effective deuterium-tritium species. Neutral deuterium or tritium atoms,
neutral molecules such as D$_2$, T$_2$, and DT, reaction products, and
impurity ions are excluded. As a number density, its value domain is $n_{DT}
\ge 0$.

items.name: radial_ion_momentum_damping_rate
items.description:
Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical decay of
a specified ion species' ordered momentum along increasing distance from the
toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Radial ion momentum damping rate quantifies relaxation of the ordered radial
component of ion [momentum](name:momentum) through collisional friction and
neoclassical viscous stresses. It is a species-level bulk-flow damping
coefficient rather than a momentum-transport flux.

The radial direction is the direction of increasing major radius in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from
the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height. In a local linear damping closure, its contribution to the radial
momentum balance is defined by:

$$
\left.\frac{\partial p_{iR}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{damping}} = -\nu_{iR} p_{iR}
$$

where $t$ is time, $p_{iR}$ is the radial bulk-flow momentum density of the
specified ion species, and $\nu_{iR}$ is this damping rate. The momentum
density is $p_{iR}=\rho_i v_{iR}$, where $\rho_i$ is the species mass
density and $v_{iR}$ is its bulk radial velocity.

The bulk velocity is the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states
of the specified species, excluding neutral particles. The damping rate is
an effective coefficient for that aggregate flow, not a sum of charge-state
rates or rates for different ion species. It excludes diffusive and
convective momentum transport and does not identify the radial direction
with the magnetic-flux-surface normal. A nonnegative rate describes damping;
zero denotes no damping from this term.

This is the radial member of the directional coefficients represented by
[ion momentum damping rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate). It differs from
[toroidal ion momentum damping
rate](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate) by acting on major-radius
flow rather than toroidal flow.

items.name: normal_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field
items.description:
Signed normal projection of the external-coil vacuum magnetic field with its
toroidally averaged component removed, evaluated on a generic control
surface.
items.documentation:
Normal non-axisymmetric magnetic field is the signed component of the
toroidally varying external-coil vacuum magnetic field normal to a generic
control surface. It is a scalar projection evaluated at points on that
surface, rather than the full magnetic-field vector.

The defining projection is

$$
B_n(R,\phi,Z)=\mathbf{B}_{\rm NA}(R,\phi,Z)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}(R,\phi,Z)
$$

where $B_n$ is the normal magnetic-field component, $\mathbf{B}_{\rm NA}$ is
the [non-axisymmetric magnetic field](name:non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field),
and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the oriented unit normal to the control surface.
The coordinates $R$, $\phi$, and $Z$ are major radius, toroidal angle, and
vertical height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This quantity applies to the external-coil vacuum contribution at each
selected point of a generic control surface, which is not assumed to be a
magnetic flux surface. Its aggregation convention is the inherited removal
of the toroidal-angle average from the vacuum field; no surface or area
average is implied.

It excludes the toroidally symmetric vacuum field and magnetic-field
contributions generated by plasma currents. It also excludes tangential
components and is distinct from cylindrical projections such as the
[vertical non-axisymmetric magnetic
field](name:vertical_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field); the normal direction
is defined by the control surface rather than by the cylindrical basis.

The scalar $B_n$ is the surface-normal component of the vector
[non-axisymmetric magnetic field](name:non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field).
Reversing the assigned orientation of the control-surface normal reverses
$B_n$, while the parent vector itself is unchanged.

Sign convention: Positive when the non-axisymmetric magnetic field points in
the direction of the chosen positive unit normal to the control surface.

items.name: parallel_ion_energy_flux
items.description:
Parallel ion energy flux is the signed component of ion energy-flux density
along the local magnetic-field direction for a specified,
charge-state-summed ion population, including convective and conductive
transport when those channels are in scope.
items.documentation:
Parallel ion energy flux is the signed component of ion energy-flux density
along the local magnetic-field direction. It gives the rate at which energy
carried by a specified ion population crosses a surface whose chosen unit
normal is the local magnetic-field direction, including convective,
conductive, or other channels only when they belong to the stated ion-energy
reservoir.

For local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, the scalar parallel
ion energy flux $F_{E,i,\parallel}$ is the projection of the ion
energy-flux-density vector $\mathbf{q}_{E,i}$ onto $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$:

$$
F_{E,i,\parallel} = \mathbf{q}_{E,i} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,i}$ is the vector density of energy transport for the
selected ion population and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector in the
direction of the local [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field) $\mathbf{B}$.

Parallel ion energy flux applies where the local magnetic-field direction is
defined and the selected ion-energy reservoir is specified. For an ion
species identified without a charge state, it is summed over all charge
states of that species; the charge-state-resolved counterpart is [parallel
ion charge-state energy flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_flux).
[Total ion energy flux](name:total_ion_energy_flux) aggregates all ion
species and charge states.

Parallel ion energy flux is a field-aligned specialization of [ion energy
flux](name:ion_energy_flux) and a species-scoped specialization of energy
flux. It is distinct from ion energy density, a volumetric energy source or
sink, ion velocity, and perpendicular, radial, or poloidal projections;
related [parallel heat flux](name:parallel_heat_flux) denotes heat transport
along the magnetic field rather than the full ion-energy reservoir unless
that reservoir is explicitly limited to heat.

Sign convention: Positive when $\mathbf{q}_{E,i}$ has a component in the
direction of the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

items.name: total_ion_power_at_inner_divertor_target
items.description:
Rate of energy deposition by all incident ion species and charge states on
the inner, high-field-side divertor target, integrated over its wetted
surface.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the ion-carried contribution to power deposited on the
inner, high-field-side divertor target. It includes the thermal energy
entering the electrostatic sheath and the directed kinetic energy acquired
by ions across the sheath potential drop, while excluding electron,
neutral-particle, photon, and halo-current contributions. It is the
ion-resolved component of ion power at the inner divertor target and is
distinct from the all-channel power at the inner divertor target.

The deposited ion power is defined by

$$
P_{i,in} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{wetted,in}}} \mathbf{q}_i \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{t}\, dA
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{in}}$ is the integrated ion power,
$A_{\mathrm{wetted,in}}$ is the wetted inner-target surface, $\mathbf{q}_i$
is the total incident ion energy-flux density summed over ion species and
charge states, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{t}$ points from the plasma toward the
target material.

items.name: toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Toroidal component of the xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity evaluated on the
plasma boundary, the last closed flux surface.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity projected onto the
geometric toroidal direction at the plasma boundary. The xenon-ion bulk
velocity is the density-weighted mean over all xenon ion charge states and
excludes thermal random motion.

$$
v_\phi = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Xe}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity in m
s$^{-1}$ and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector of the
right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ frame. The plasma
boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface. This local value is
distinct from the flux-surface average
toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_xenon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when $v_\phi$ points in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: volume_averaged_total_ion_density
items.description:
Volume-averaged total ion number density over the confined plasma volume,
summing all ion species and charge states and including thermal and
non-thermal ion populations.
items.documentation:
Volume-averaged total ion density is the aggregate ion number density
averaged over the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux
surface. It includes all ion species, resolved charge states, and thermal
and non-thermal ion populations; it excludes electrons and neutral
particles.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{i,\mathrm{total}} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{i,\mathrm{total}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_{i,\mathrm{total}}$ is the volume-averaged density,
$n_{i,\mathrm{total}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local [total ion
density](name:total_ion_number_density) in m$^{-3}$, $V_p$ is the confined
plasma volume in m$^3$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $dV$ is the volume
element. This is a density average, not the total ion inventory. Unlike
[volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density), it
aggregates all ion species rather than one selected species.

items.name: fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Fast-electron collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum
transfer rate per unit volume delivered to fast electrons through Coulomb
collisions.
items.documentation:
Fast-electron collisional torque density is the vector rate of
angular-momentum transfer to the fast-electron population through Coulomb
momentum exchange with other plasma species. It is the fast-population
specialization of [electron collisional torque
density](name:electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

For position vector $\mathbf{r}$ relative to the chosen torque origin and
collisional force density $\mathbf{F}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ acting on fast
electrons, the torque density is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r}) = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{F}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the fast-electron
collisional torque density, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector, and
$\mathbf{F}_{e,f}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density.

The quantity may be resolved by orbit class or directional component,
including co-passing fast-electron collisional torque density and [toroidal
fast-electron collisional torque
density](name:toroidal_fast_particle_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons).
It excludes torque from noncollisional forces and is distinct from
[thermal-electron collisional torque
density](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when each torque-density component points along
the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ basis.

items.name: y_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
items.description:
Y component of the unit vector along the minor axis of an elliptic shatter
cone, resolved in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
The minor-axis unit vector specifies one orientation of the elliptic shatter
cone. This quantity is its signed projection onto the Cartesian y direction,
complementing the [x minor-axis
component](name:x_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) and [z minor-axis
component](name:z_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone).

The component is defined by

$$
u_y = \mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{minor}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{minor}}$ is the unit vector along the
shatter-cone minor axis and $\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the y-directed unit vector
in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame. The
complete minor-axis vector has unit norm, so its components satisfy $u_x^2 +
u_y^2 + u_z^2 = 1$.

items.name: thickness_of_plasma_facing_component
items.description:
Through-material geometric separation between a plasma-facing component’s
exposed surface and its opposite material boundary, evaluated at the
component midplane.
items.documentation:
The thickness is the through-material dimension of a plasma-facing component
at its midplane, separating the plasma-exposed surface from the opposite
material boundary. It is measured along the local thickness direction normal
to the exposed surface.

$$
t_{\mathrm{PFC}} = d_{\perp}\left(S_{\mathrm{plasma}}, S_{\mathrm{back}}\right)\big|_{\mathrm{midplane}}
$$

Here, $t_{\mathrm{PFC}}$ is the component thickness, $d_{\perp}$ is the
through-material normal separation, and $S_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ and
$S_{\mathrm{back}}$ are the exposed and opposite material surfaces,
respectively.

This is a geometric material dimension for the specified midplane section;
it is not a plasma-to-wall separation such as the gap at the plasma
boundary, nor a surface thermal quantity.

items.name: ion_charge_state_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective advective velocity vector governing particle transport of a
specified ion charge state, with projections for distinct plasma transport
directions.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective advective velocity vector assigned to the
particle population of a specified ion charge state. It describes the
velocity that multiplies the charge-state number density to produce the
convective part of particle transport, including the applicable thermal and
nonthermal populations.

The convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s,\mathrm{conv}} = n_s \mathbf{v}_s
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective particle
flux, $n_s$ is the number density of the specified ion charge state, and
$\mathbf{v}_s$ is this convection-velocity vector. The total particle flux
may additionally contain a diffusive contribution, which is excluded here.

The vector may be resolved into directional quantities, including the
[poloidal ion charge-state convection
velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) and [parallel
ion charge-state convection
velocity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity). It is
distinct from [ion momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_momentum_convection_velocity), which describes advective
transport of aggregate ion momentum.

Sign convention: Positive for the radial transport component when directed
outward toward the last closed flux surface; negative when directed inward
toward the magnetic axis.

items.name: current_due_to_non_inductive_current_drive
items.description:
Net plasma current sustained by non-inductive mechanisms, including
bootstrap, neutral-beam, and wave-driven contributions, rather than
inductive electric-field drive.
items.documentation:
Non-inductive plasma current is the net plasma-current contribution
sustained without inductive electric-field drive. It combines all
non-inductive mechanisms, retaining the signs of their contributions rather
than summing their magnitudes.

The aggregate current is defined by

$$
I_{\mathrm{ni}} = \sum_{k\in\mathcal{N}} I_k
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{ni}}$ is the non-inductive current, $\mathcal{N}$ is the
set of non-inductive mechanisms, $k$ identifies a mechanism, and $I_k$ is
its signed current contribution. All terms use the same projection and
integration region. The sum includes bootstrap,
[neutral-beam-driven](name:current_due_to_neutral_beam_injection), and
wave-driven current contributions.

The unqualified global value is the toroidal current integrated over the
full plasma poloidal cross-section, not the integral of the field-parallel
current density. The right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R, \phi, Z)$, where
$R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.
Projection- and region-qualified members retain those restrictions: the
[parallel cumulative current inside a flux
surface](name:parallel_cumulative_inside_flux_surface_current_due_to_non_inductive_current_drive)
uses the field-aligned projection and the enclosed integration region rather
than the global toroidal definition.

The [inductively driven Ohmic
current](name:current_due_to_ohmic_current_drive) is excluded. This
exclusion concerns the attributed current contribution; it does not require
the total plasma loop voltage to vanish or the plasma to be in steady state.

Sign convention: Positive when the global toroidal current flows in the
direction of increasing $\phi$, counterclockwise when viewed from above.

items.name: fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Fast-particle power due to collisions is the volume-integrated Coulomb
collisional power transferred from the fast, non-Maxwellian particle
population to the bulk electron population.
items.documentation:
Fast-particle power due to collisions is the net rate at which Coulomb
collisions transfer kinetic energy from the fast, non-Maxwellian particle
population to the bulk electron population. It is the plasma-volume integral
of the local collisional energy-transfer density for this donor-recipient
population pair.

The volume-integrated transfer is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast}\to e}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{fast}\to e}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fast}\to e}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the fast-particle power
due to collisions, $p_{\mathrm{fast}\to e}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x})$ is
the local Coulomb collisional energy-transfer density from the fast-particle
population to the bulk electron population, $\mathbf{x}$ is position,
$V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume, and $dV$ is the differential
volume element.

The quantity applies to all fast particles belonging to the non-Maxwellian
population in the plasma, including all orbit classes and any unresolved
subdivisions such as source, energy, pitch, species, or charge-state groups.
Its aggregation convention is a sum over all included fast-particle
subpopulations and over the plasma volume.

It excludes collisional power transferred from fast particles to bulk ion
populations, collisional exchange internal to the bulk thermal populations,
non-collisional heating, field or wave power, launched or generator power,
and power retained in or lost with fast particles rather than deposited in
bulk electrons.

This quantity is the fast-particle donor component of [thermal electron
power due to collisions](name:thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions) when
that electron power is decomposed by source population. Summing analogous
recipient-species components gives the total Coulomb collisional energy loss
of the fast-particle population.

Sign convention: Positive when net Coulomb collisional energy transfer is
from the fast-particle population to the bulk electron population.

items.name: helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of helium-3 ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the
local particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux
surface and summed over charge states.
items.documentation:
Number density of helium-3 ions at the plasma boundary is the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume for the helium-3 ion population
evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is
the limiting closed magnetic flux surface, or separatrix, separating
confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off-layer region.

The local charge-state-summed helium-3 number density is the zeroth velocity
moment of the helium-3 ion distribution functions at a boundary point:

$$
n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \sum_{q=1}^{2} \int f_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He},q}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 ion number density,
$\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux surface, $t$ is
time, $q$ is the helium-3 ionic charge state, $f_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He},q}$ is
the phase-space distribution function for that charge state, $\mathbf{v}$ is
ion velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to helium-3 ions, whose nuclei contain
three nucleons, and includes all ionized charge states from singly charged
through fully stripped helium-3. It excludes neutral helium-3, other helium
isotopes, and other plasma species. The value is local at the boundary and
is not averaged over the boundary surface or over a volume.

It is the helium-3-specific instance of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related
flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary represents the
average of this local helium-3 ion density over the same last closed
magnetic flux surface rather than its value at a boundary point.

items.name: hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron hydrogen source rate delivered to the
plasma vessel by gas injection systems; each hydrogen atom contributes one
equivalent-electron count.
items.documentation:
The hydrogen source rate due to gas injection characterizes the
instantaneous rate at which neutral hydrogen atoms are admitted to the
plasma vessel by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count
rate. Because hydrogen has atomic number one, each atom contributes one
equivalent-electron count.

The defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{H}} = Z_{\mathrm{H}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}} = \dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}, \qquad Z_{\mathrm{H}} = 1
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the neutral hydrogen-atom delivery rate in atoms
per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the hydrogen atomic number. This is the
hydrogen component of the total [source rate due to gas
injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection). Its time integral gives
the accumulated hydrogen inventory [accumulated hydrogen count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection).

Sign convention: Positive when hydrogen gas is being delivered into the
vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron inventory.

items.name: neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Fickian transport coefficient relating a neutral population's
density-normalized diffusive thermal-energy flux to its temperature
gradient, without selecting a direction or internal state.
items.documentation:
The neutral energy diffusion coefficient characterizes gradient-driven
diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by a specified neutral
population. It is the neutral-population specialization of the [energy
diffusion coefficient](name:energy_diffusion_coefficient), without selecting
a transport direction or resolving an internal state.

For a local isotropic diffusive closure, the defining relation is:

$$
\frac{\mathbf{Q}_{0,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_0} = -D_{0,W}\,\nabla T_0
$$

where $D_{0,W}$ is the neutral energy diffusion coefficient,
$\mathbf{Q}_{0,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the neutral diffusive thermal-energy flux,
$n_0$ is the neutral number density, $T_0$ is the neutral temperature
expressed as thermal energy, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient. The
subscripts $0$ and $W$ identify the neutral population and energy channel,
respectively. The minus sign gives transport down the temperature gradient
for a positive coefficient.

This is a population-level coefficient, with the included neutral internal
states treated collectively rather than resolved separately. It is not a sum
of internal-state diffusion coefficients. The defining flux excludes
convective and advective contributions to the total neutral thermal-energy
flux, and the coefficient describes energy transport rather than particle
transport.

The [radial](name:radial_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient),
[poloidal](name:poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient), and
[parallel](name:parallel_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient)
specializations apply the flux-gradient definition to their corresponding
directional projections. Their coefficients need not be equal; the
direction-agnostic parent does not impose isotropy on these specializations.
The [effective neutral energy diffusion
coefficient](name:effective_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient) retains
the same density-normalized flux-gradient interpretation.

items.name: radial_outline_of_flux_surface
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of a point on a poloidal magnetic-flux level-set
contour, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Radial outline of a flux surface is the major-radius coordinate $R$ of a
point on a contour of constant poloidal magnetic flux. The contour is
described in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For a point whose Cartesian coordinates are $(x,y,z)$ in the right-handed
Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$, the
corresponding major-radius coordinate is

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are Cartesian coordinates in the plane perpendicular to
the toroidal symmetry axis.

This quantity is the radial coordinate component of the flux-surface
outline, paired with the vertical outline of a flux surface. It is a
specialization of [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate) to points on a
poloidal magnetic-flux level set and does not denote the flux label, a
flux-surface-normal displacement, or the radial component of a vector field.

items.name: helium_3_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Particle number density of helium-3 ions evaluated on the flux surface
assigned to an internal transport barrier, summed over all helium-3 ion
charge states and excluding neutral helium-3.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of helium-3 ions evaluated on the flux surface
assigned to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the
helium-3-ion population at that flux-surface location. Helium-3
(${}^3\mathrm{He}$, mass number $A = 3$, atomic number $Z = 2$) has a
nucleus with two protons and one neutron; at species level this quantity
includes singly ionized ${}^3\mathrm{He}^{+}$ and fully ionized
${}^3\mathrm{He}^{2+}$ and excludes neutral ${}^3\mathrm{He}$ atoms.

The charge-state-summed particle number density is defined by

$$
n_{{}^3\mathrm{He},\mathrm{ITB}} = \left.\lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{\Delta N_{{}^3\mathrm{He}^{+}} + \Delta N_{{}^3\mathrm{He}^{2+}}}{\Delta V}\right|_{\mathrm{ITB}}
$$

where $n_{{}^3\mathrm{He},\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the helium-3 ion number density
at the internal-transport-barrier reference flux surface, $\Delta
N_{{}^3\mathrm{He}^{+}}$ and $\Delta N_{{}^3\mathrm{He}^{2+}}$ are the
counted singly ionized and fully ionized helium-3 ions in the volume element
$\Delta V$, and the vertical bar denotes evaluation at that assigned flux
surface.

This is a particle number density, not a charge-weighted density; both
ionization stages contribute one counted ion per particle. It is the
internal-transport-barrier evaluation of [helium-3
density](name:helium_3_density) and the helium-3-specific member of [density
at the internal transport
barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier), distinct from broader
ion aggregates such as ion density at the internal transport barrier and
from isotope counterparts such as [helium-4 density at the internal
transport barrier](name:helium_4_density_at_internal_transport_barrier). The
internal transport barrier is the designated flux-surface location where
reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep density gradients.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_density
items.description:
Number density of neutral particles of a specified species in one internal
quantum state, including both thermal and nonthermal velocity populations.
items.documentation:
Number density of neutral

The density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the neutral-state
distribution:

$$
n_{s,a}^{0} = \int f_{s,a}^{0}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v = n_{s,a}^{0,\mathrm{th}} + n_{s,a}^{0,\mathrm{nt}}
$$

where $n_{s,a}^{0}$ is the total neutral-state number density, $s$ labels
the neutral species, $a$ labels its selected internal quantum state, and the
superscript $0$ denotes electrical neutrality. The function $f_{s,a}^{0}$ is
the velocity-space number distribution for that species and state, and
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity. The contributions
$n_{s,a}^{0,\mathrm{th}}$ and $n_{s,a}^{0,\mathrm{nt}}$ are the [thermal
neutral internal-state density](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_density)
and the [fast neutral internal-state number
density](name:fast_neutral_internal_state_number_density), respectively,
evaluated at the same location and time.

The quantity is summed over velocity populations, not over species or
internal states. Charged particles and neutral particles in other internal
states are excluded. The definition applies locally or to a flux-surface
average in the closed-field-line region; an evaluation at the outboard
equatorial midplane in the scrape-off layer is local rather than
flux-surface averaged.

Summing this state-resolved density over all internal states of the same
neutral species gives the [neutral-species
density](name:neutral_species_density). The thermal contribution alone
excludes the nonthermal particles included here.

items.name: ion_average_temperature_at_post_sawtooth_crash
items.description:
Density-weighted mean random kinetic energy of all ion species and charge
states, expressed as an energy-equivalent temperature after a sawtooth
crash.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the energy-equivalent temperature of the ion population
after a sawtooth crash, averaged over every included ion species and charge
state. It characterizes the mean thermal energy of the post-crash ions and
is distinct from a temperature assigned to one species or charge state.

$$
T_i = \frac{\sum_s n_s T_s}{\sum_s n_s}
$$

where $T_i$ is the averaged ion temperature, $T_s$ is the temperature of ion
species and charge state $s$, and $n_s$ is its number density. The summation
includes all ion species and charge states in the defined population. The
corresponding general quantity is [ion average
temperature](name:ion_average_temperature), while [ion average temperature
at an internal transport
barrier](name:ion_average_temperature_at_internal_transport_barrier) applies
the same averaging concept at a different plasma locus.

items.name: deuterium_deuterium_neutron_source_rate_due_to_beam_beam_fusion
items.description:
Volume-integrated neutron production rate from beam-beam fusion between
deuterons originating from fast beam populations in the plasma.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the total neutron production rate associated with the
neutron-producing deuterium–deuterium beam–beam fusion branch. It represents
reactions between deuterons belonging to beam populations, rather than
reactions involving the thermal deuteron population.

The rate is defined as the volume integral of the local beam–beam
neutron-production rate:

$$
S_{DD,bb} = \int_{V_{\rm plasma}} \varepsilon_{DD,bb}(\mathbf{x})\,d^3\mathbf{x}
$$

where $S_{DD,bb}$ is the integrated neutron production rate,
$\varepsilon_{DD,bb}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local neutron-production rate from
beam–beam deuterium–deuterium fusion, $V_{\rm plasma}$ is the plasma volume
included in the aggregation, and $\mathbf{x}$ is the spatial position. The
subscripts $DD$ and $bb$ identify the deuterium–deuterium reaction and
beam–beam fusion branch, respectively.

The scope is restricted to the neutron-producing deuterium–deuterium branch
and to reactions between beam-origin deuterons. It is a single
volume-integrated total over the plasma and excludes thermal
deuterium–deuterium fusion, beam–thermal fusion, other fusion reaction
channels, and the local volumetric emissivity represented by
[deuterium-deuterium emissivity due to
fusion](name:deuterium_deuterium_emissivity_due_to_fusion).

This branch-resolved rate contributes to neutron flux, which aggregates
neutron production over the applicable fusion reaction channels. It is
distinct from deuterium-deuterium neutron source rate due to thermal fusion,
whose corresponding contribution arises from the thermonuclear
deuterium–deuterium branch.

items.name: vertical_bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity
items.description:
Projection along the toroidal symmetry axis of the mean translational
velocity of neutral particles in one specified internal quantum or energy
state.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the vertical component of the bulk translational flow of a
neutral species occupying one specified internal quantum or energy state.
Vertical denotes the direction parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position.

At a given position, the component is the vertical projection of the first
velocity moment:

$$
u_{0,a,Z}=\hat{\mathbf z}\cdot\mathbf u_{0,a}=\frac{\int (\mathbf v\cdot\hat{\mathbf z})f_{0,a}(\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\int f_{0,a}(\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $u_{0,a,Z}$ is the vertical bulk velocity, $\mathbf u_{0,a}$ is the
[bulk neutral internal-state
velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity), $\hat{\mathbf z}$ is
the unit vector toward increasing vertical position, $\mathbf v$ is particle
velocity, and $f_{0,a}$ is the local velocity distribution of the selected
neutral species in internal state $a$. The subscript $0$ denotes neutral
particles, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The average is taken over particle velocities within the specified species
and internal state; distinct internal states and neutral species are not
combined. Bulk denotes mean translational flow, without imposing a hot- or
cold-population selection. This signed component is not the flow-vector
magnitude, a random thermal spread, or a particle flux; unlike a
mechanism-specific effective transport velocity, it is not restricted to one
transport contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when the neutral bulk flow points toward
increasing $Z$.

items.name: deposited_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_halo_current
items.description:
Deposited power at a divertor target due to halo current is the electrical
work rate delivered to one divertor target by halo current crossing its
plasma-facing surface.
items.documentation:
Deposited power at a divertor target due to halo current is the electrical
work rate delivered to one divertor target by halo current crossing the
plasma-facing target surface. Halo current is current in the edge or
scrape-off-layer plasma that closes through conducting plasma-facing
structures; this quantity selects only its contribution to current-driven
target loading.

For a target surface with defined local current density and potential drop,
the target-surface definition is:

$$
P_{\mathrm{halo},t} = \int_{A_t} j_{\mathrm{halo},n}^{\mathrm{in}}(\mathbf{r})\,\Delta\Phi_t(\mathbf{r})\,dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{halo},t}$ is this deposited power, $A_t$ is the portion of
the plasma-facing target surface intercepted by halo current, $dA$ is a
target-surface area element, $j_{\mathrm{halo},n}^{\mathrm{in}}$ is the
conventional halo-current density projected on the local unit normal
directed from the plasma into the target material, and $\Delta\Phi_t =
\Phi_{\mathrm{plasma}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the local
plasma-to-target potential drop.

The surface integral of $j_{\mathrm{halo},n}^{\mathrm{in}}$ over $A_t$ is
the halo-current contribution to [current at divertor
target](name:current_at_divertor_target). This quantity excludes the
conductive, convective, radiative, and neutral-particle target-power
channels, and excludes current-driven target power not produced by halo
current; together with other current-driven components it is part of [power
at divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target), while sums over divertor
targets contribute to power of divertor. It is zero when no halo-current
electrical work is deposited on the target; positive values denote net
energy deposition on that target.

Sign convention: Positive when conventional halo current crosses from the
plasma into the target along the plasma-to-material surface normal across a
positive plasma-to-target potential drop.

items.name: spectral_efficiency_of_filter
items.description:
Wavelength-resolved probability that a photon incident on a diagnostic
filter produces a registered detection event after wavelength-dependent
transmission and detection losses.
items.documentation:
The wavelength-resolved filter efficiency is the conditional probability
that a photon arriving at the filter input with wavelength $\lambda$
produces a registered detection event. It includes the wavelength-dependent
transmission and conversion losses of the filter, optical path, detector,
and readout chain, and is distinct from material absorptivity alone.

$$
\eta_{\mathrm{filter}}(\lambda)=P(\mathrm{registered\ detection}\mid\mathrm{photon\ incident\ at\ wavelength\ }\lambda)
$$

Here, $\lambda$ is the photon wavelength and $P$ denotes a conditional
probability. The parent efficiency of filter is the
incident-spectrum-weighted average of this response, with weighting supplied
by the incident spectral flux over the relevant wavelength range.
Consequently, this quantity is dimensionless and bounded from 0 to 1.

items.name: atomic_number
items.description:
Atomic number is the nuclear proton count that identifies an element and
remains unchanged across its isotopes and ionization states.
items.documentation:
Atomic number

The defining relation to nuclear electric charge is:

$$
Z = \frac{Q_{\mathrm{nuc}}}{e}
$$

where $Z$ is the atomic number, $Q_{\mathrm{nuc}}$ is the nuclear electric
charge, and $e$ is the positive elementary charge.

The value applies to one elemental nucleus, whether present in a neutral
atom, an ion, or a molecular constituent. It is a positive integer, not a
sum or average over nuclei or charge states. For a molecular species,
[atomic count](name:atomic_count) separately specifies how many atoms of
that element constitute one particle.

For a fully stripped ion, the ionic charge number equals $Z$; partial
ionization changes the ionic charge but not the atomic number. Thus, atomic
number differs from the [average charge number](name:average_charge_number),
which depends on the charge-state distribution. The [ion atomic
number](name:ion_atomic_number) is this same nuclear property specialized to
an ion species.

items.name: ordinary_mode_fraction_of_electron_cyclotron_beam
items.description:
Fraction of the launched power of an electron-cyclotron beam carried by the
ordinary polarization mode, ranging from pure X-mode to pure O-mode.
items.documentation:
The ordinary-mode power fraction quantifies the share of one launched
electron-cyclotron beam carried by the ordinary (O) polarization mode rather
than the extraordinary (X) mode.

It is defined by the ratio

$$
f_O = \frac{P_O}{P_{\mathrm{EC}}}
$$

where $f_O$ is the ordinary-mode power fraction, $P_O$ is the launched power
in the ordinary mode, and $P_{\mathrm{EC}}$ is the total launched power of
the electron-cyclotron beam.

The quantity applies to a single electron-cyclotron beam and uses launched
beam power aggregated over the beam's ordinary-mode content. It excludes
power from other beams and does not represent the total launched power
itself. Values of $f_O=1$ and $f_O=0$ denote pure ordinary-mode and pure
extraordinary-mode launch, respectively.

This power partition is distinct from [polarization ellipticity of a
polarimeter beam](name:polarization_ellipticity_of_polarimeter_beam), which
describes the shape and handedness of a polarization ellipse rather than the
O-mode fraction of an electron-cyclotron beam.

items.name: volume_of_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Volume enclosed by the plasma boundary, representing the total
confined-plasma region inside the last closed magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the geometric volume of the confined plasma enclosed by the
plasma boundary, identified with the last closed magnetic flux surface. It
represents the full enclosed region rather than a local flux-surface shell
or material volume.

The volume is defined by

$$
V = \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{plasma}}} d^3\mathbf{x}
$$

where $V$ is the enclosed plasma volume, $\Omega_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the
spatial domain inside the plasma boundary, and $d^3\mathbf{x}$ is the
differential volume element at position $\mathbf{x}$.

The integration domain is the entire confined-plasma region bounded by the
last closed magnetic flux surface, and the result is the total volume
aggregated over that domain. It excludes regions outside the plasma boundary
and volumes belonging to material structures or other non-confined regions.

This quantity is the terminal enclosed value of [volume of a flux
surface](name:volume_of_flux_surface) when the flux surface coincides with
the plasma boundary. It provides the integration domain for volume-averaged
quantities such as [volume-averaged ion
temperature](name:volume_averaged_ion_temperature).

items.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate
items.description:
Inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical damping of ordered
poloidal flow momentum carried by ions of one specified species and charge
state.
items.documentation:
The poloidal ion charge-state momentum damping rate quantifies how rapidly
collisions and neoclassical viscous stresses relax the ordered poloidal
[momentum](name:momentum) of a specified ion species and charge state. The
poloidal direction is tangent to a magnetic flux surface within a plane
containing the toroidal symmetry axis.

In a linear relaxation closure, its contribution to the poloidal
momentum-density balance is:

$$
\left.\frac{\partial \delta g_{s,\mathrm{p}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{damp}} = -\nu_{s,\mathrm{p}}\,\delta g_{s,\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $\delta g_{s,\mathrm{p}}$ is the departure of the poloidal flow
momentum density from its relaxed value, $s$ identifies the ion species and
charge state, $\nu_{s,\mathrm{p}}$ is this damping rate, $t$ is time, and
the subscript $\mathrm{p}$ denotes the poloidal direction. The restriction
labeled $\mathrm{damp}$ includes only the relaxation contribution. For a
fixed positive rate, this contribution produces exponential decay of the
departure from the relaxed value.

This is the poloidal directional coefficient of [ion charge-state momentum
damping rate](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate). It applies to
one specified charge state, without summation or averaging over charge
states; [poloidal ion momentum damping
rate](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate) instead describes the
species-level bulk-flow relaxation.

The rate describes local momentum relaxation, not transport driven by a
spatial gradient. It is therefore distinct from [poloidal ion charge-state
momentum diffusivity], which governs diffusive momentum transport. It does
not include convective transport or externally applied momentum sources.

items.name: parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density
items.description:
Dimensionless field-aligned component of the charge-weighted first velocity
moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution, normalized to a reference
current-density scale.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the parallel component of the normalized gyrocenter
current-density perturbation. It represents the charge-weighted first moment
of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution along the local magnetic-field
direction and is the field-aligned component of [normalized gyrocenter
perturbed current
density](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density).

$$
J_{parallel,g}^{(s)} = \frac{q_s}{J_{\rm ref}} \int v_\parallel\,\delta g_s\,d^3v
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of species $s$, $v_\parallel$ is its velocity
along the local magnetic field, $\delta g_s$ is the perturbed gyrocenter
distribution function, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and
$J_{\rm ref}$ is the reference current-density scale. The underlying
unnormalized moment is the corresponding perturbed gyrocenter current
density. For a linear eigenmode, the quantity may be complex, with its phase
defined by the eigenmode convention.

Sign convention: Positive when the perturbed gyrocenter current density
points along the local magnetic field.

items.name: neutral_state_diamagnetic_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless coefficient scaling the free-streaming bound on diamagnetic
momentum flux for a specified neutral species and internal state, limiting
flux magnitude without reversing its direction.
items.documentation:
This coefficient scales the collisionless free-streaming bound on the
diamagnetic component of [momentum](name:momentum) flux carried by a
specified neutral species in a specified internal state. It controls the
admissible flux magnitude in a state-resolved fluid transport closure.

Its cap-setting role is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{\max} = \alpha\,\Pi_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\alpha$ is this coefficient, $\Pi_{\max}$ is the maximum admissible
diamagnetic momentum-flux magnitude, and $\Pi_{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the
nonnegative collisionless free-streaming reference magnitude for the same
momentum component and neutral-state population.

The coefficient applies separately to the selected neutral species and
internal state; it is neither summed nor averaged over species or states.
Limiting reduces the flux magnitude without reversing its direction. This
coefficient is not a momentum diffusivity or a neutral-particle drift
velocity, and its definition does not prescribe a particular interpolation
between unrestricted and limited fluxes.

It is the neutral-state-resolved specialization of the [diamagnetic momentum
flux limiter
coefficient](name:diamagnetic_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), within the
broader [momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) family. Unlike the
[neutral-state particle flux limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient), it
bounds momentum transport rather than particle-number transport.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description:
Helium-4 abundance ratio formed from mean densities inside the last closed
flux surface, comparing the charge-state-summed helium-4 ion density with
the electron density after each density is volume averaged.
items.documentation:
Helium-4 abundance ratio formed from mean densities inside the last closed
flux surface is the quotient of the volume-averaged helium-4 ion number
density and the volume-averaged electron number density. It is a global
isotope-abundance measure for ionized helium-4 relative to electrons in the
plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface.

The ratio is defined from independent volume averages over the same enclosed
plasma volume:

$$
f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V} = \frac{\langle n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}\rangle_V}{\langle n_e\rangle_V}, \qquad \langle n_s\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{LCFS}}\int_{V_\mathrm{LCFS}} n_s(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V}$ is this helium-4 abundance ratio, the
superscript $V$ denotes formation from volume averages, $\langle
n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged helium-4
density](name:volume_averaged_helium_4_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is
the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_s(\mathbf{x})$ is the
local number density of species $s$ at position $\mathbf{x}$,
$V_\mathrm{LCFS}$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux
surface, and $dV$ is an element of that volume. For $s={}^4\mathrm{He}$,
$n_s$ is the local helium-4 ion number density summed over all ion charge
states; for $s=e$, $n_s$ is the local electron number density.

The semantic scope is species-level helium-4 ion density inside the last
closed flux surface. The helium-4 numerator is summed over all ion charge
states before averaging, while neutral helium-4 atoms and helium isotopes
other than helium-4 are excluded. Because the numerator and denominator are
averaged separately, this quantity is not the volume average of the local
ratio $n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}/n_e$.

For fully stripped helium-4 ions in a quasi-neutral plasma, $2
f_{{}^4\mathrm{He},e}^{V}$ represents the helium-4 ion contribution to the
electron charge balance, apart from contributions of other ions and
departures from full stripping. The isotope analog is [ratio of
volume-averaged helium-3 density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_3_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
and the analogous elemental abundance quantity is [ratio of volume-averaged
neon density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_neon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).
It is related to ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 ion density to electron
density by the shared helium-4 numerator species, while this name explicitly
normalizes by the independently volume-averaged electron density.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Kinematic coefficient for down-gradient diffusion along the magnetic field
of field-parallel flow momentum carried by ions of one species and charge
state.
items.documentation:
Parallel ion charge-state momentum diffusivity governs diffusive
redistribution along the magnetic field of field-parallel flow
[momentum](name:momentum) carried by a specified ion species and charge
state. It is the field-parallel directional component of [ion charge-state
momentum diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity).

In a local Fick-law closure, the diffusive momentum flux is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\chi_{s,\parallel}\,\mathbf{b}\cdot\nabla g_{s,\parallel}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state,
$\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the flux of field-parallel momentum
along the magnetic field, $\chi_{s,\parallel}$ is this diffusivity, and
$g_{s,\parallel}$ is the selected state's field-parallel momentum density.
The unit vector $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ follows the local
magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient. The
momentum density is $g_{s,\parallel}=m_s n_s v_{s,\parallel}$, where $m_s$
is the ion mass, $n_s$ is the charge-state number density, and
$v_{s,\parallel}$ is the mean field-parallel flow velocity.

The coefficient is resolved for one charge state, not summed or averaged
over charge states. It describes only the diffusive contribution, excluding
convective momentum transport, residual stress, and external momentum
sources. Unlike [poloidal ion charge-state momentum diffusivity], which
describes transport along a poloidal arc on a flux surface, this coefficient
follows the local magnetic-field direction.

items.name: toroidal_trapped_fast_current_density
items.description:
Toroidal current density is the flux-surface-averaged charge flux carried by
magnetically trapped fast particles in the toroidal direction, excluding
electron and thermal-ion back-currents.
items.documentation:
Toroidal current density carried by trapped fast particles is the
magnetic-flux-surface average of the toroidal projection of [trapped
fast-particle current density](name:trapped_fast_current_density). It
represents conventional electric-charge transport by nonthermal particles on
magnetically trapped guiding-center orbits.

The averaged projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\phi,\mathrm{fast,tr}} = \left\langle \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{fast,tr}}\cdot\hat{\phi}\right\rangle
$$

where $j_{\phi,\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged toroidal
trapped-fast-particle current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{fast,tr}}$ is
the local trapped-fast-particle current-density vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the
toroidal unit vector, and angle brackets denote the magnetic-flux-surface
average. The direction $\hat{\phi}$ follows increasing toroidal angle in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Only the trapped portion of the specified species' fast-particle
distribution contributes; multiple included fast populations of that species
are superposed linearly. Passing fast particles and compensating electron
and thermal-ion back-currents are excluded. This is a signed,
surface-averaged component, not a local value, a vector magnitude, or the
total plasma [current density](name:current_density).

Unlike this direct fast-particle contribution, [toroidal trapped current
density](name:toroidal_trapped_current_density) also includes the
collisional drag back-current attributed to trapped particles.

Sign convention: Positive when the flux-surface-averaged conventional charge
transport by trapped fast particles follows increasing $\phi$,
counter-clockwise when viewed from above.

items.name: weight_of_interferometer_beam
items.description:
Weight of an interferometer beam is the scalar factor assigned to the
residual for one interferometer beam, controlling how strongly that beam's
line-integrated electron-density constraint contributes to a weighted
objective. It applies per beam, not to an entire interferometer system.
items.documentation:
Weight of an interferometer beam is the scalar factor assigned to the
residual for one interferometer beam in a weighted objective. The residual
is associated with that beam's line-integrated electron-density constraint,
so the weight controls that beam's relative influence among simultaneously
weighted constraints.

For a quadratic weighted objective, the contribution from one beam is
represented by:

$$
\Phi_b = w_b r_b^2
$$

where $w_b$ is the weight of the interferometer beam, $r_b$ is the residual
between the modeled and reference line-integrated electron density for the
same beam, and $\Phi_b$ is that beam's contribution to the objective.

The scope is a single interferometer beam. No summation, averaging, or
normalization over multiple beams is implied; a set of beams has separate
weights and separate residual contributions. This quantity is not the
line-integrated electron density, not the residual itself, not an
uncertainty, and not a weight for a whole interferometer system or for other
constraint types.

The [equilibrium weight of an interferometer
beam](name:equilibrium_weight_of_interferometer_beam) is the
equilibrium-specific specialization of this parent quantity. Changing $w_b$
changes only the relative contribution of the corresponding beam term in the
objective; it does not change the definition of the beam residual.

items.name: fast_ion_power_due_to_charge_exchange
items.description:
Volume-integrated kinetic-energy loss rate from the confined fast-ion
population due to charge exchange.
items.documentation:
Volume-integrated kinetic-energy loss rate from the confined fast-ion
population due to charge exchange is the rate at which electron-transfer
reactions with neutral particles remove kinetic energy from confined fast
ions. The removed energy is not Coulomb energy transfer to plasma particles;
it is a loss from the confined fast-ion energy content.

The volume integral is taken over the corresponding local loss-rate density:

$$
P_{\mathrm{CX},f} = \int_V p_{\mathrm{CX},f}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{CX},f}$ is the fast-ion power due to charge exchange,
$p_{\mathrm{CX},f}(\mathbf{x})$ is the fast-ion power density due to charge
exchange, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $V$ is the region over which the
confined fast-ion population is defined. Locally, $p_{\mathrm{CX},f}$ is the
charge-exchange event-rate density weighted by the kinetic energy removed
from the confined fast-ion population per event, summed over all included
fast-ion species and charge states.

This quantity excludes Coulomb collisional energy transfer, ionization
losses not involving charge exchange, prompt orbit loss, power that was
never absorbed into the fast-ion population, and charge-exchange loss
assigned solely to thermal ions. It is the fast-ion component of ion power
due to charge exchange and contributes to the broader power due to charge
exchange; in a fast-ion energy balance written with positive gains, this
loss magnitude enters as a sink.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity
items.description:
Effective diagonal diffusivity for down-gradient transport of energy carried
by neutral particles in a specified internal state along poloidal flux
surfaces.
items.documentation:
The poloidal component of the [effective neutral internal-state energy
diffusivity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity)
tensor expresses effective Fickian transport of energy carried by neutral
particles occupying a specified internal state. It acts along the poloidal
tangent to a flux surface, rather than along the magnetic-field direction.

$$
\Gamma_{E,\theta}=-D^{\mathrm{eff}}_{E,\theta}\left.\frac{\partial e_{n,s}}{\partial \ell_\theta}\right|_{\rho,\phi}
$$

Here $\Gamma_{E,\theta}$ is the poloidal energy flux,
$D^{\mathrm{eff}}_{E,\theta}$ is this diffusivity, $e_{n,s}$ is the energy
density of neutral particles in internal state $s$, and $\ell_\theta$ is
distance along the poloidal tangent. The coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$
are the flux-surface, poloidal-angle, and toroidal-angle coordinates; the
derivative is taken at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$.

This effective coefficient represents the net phenomenological response, not
a single microscopic mechanism. Its directional and state scope is shared by
the [poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient),
while the parallel counterpart resolves transport along magnetic field
lines.

items.name: fast_ion_charge_state_absorbed_wave_power
items.description:
Volume-integrated electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly to fast
ions in one specified ion charge state, excluding collisional energy
exchange.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the direct electromagnetic-wave energy transfer rate to the
fast, non-thermal ions belonging to one specified charge state, integrated
over the full plasma volume.

The defining relation is

$$
P_{q,\mathrm{wave}} = \int_V p_{q,\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $P_{q,\mathrm{wave}}$ is the absorbed wave power for charge state $q$,
$p_{q,\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r})$ is its local wave-power deposition
density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $V$ is the full plasma volume.

This is a charge-state-resolved component of ion charge-state absorbed wave
power: it excludes power transferred subsequently through Coulomb collisions
and is not the cumulative value inside a selected flux surface, which is
represented by [fast ion charge-state power at inside flux
surface](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

items.name: z_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
items.description:
Signed component along the z axis of the unit vector defining an
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror's translation direction or rotation axis
at its home position, in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
Signed component along the z axis of the unit vector defining an
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror's translation direction or rotation axis
at its home position is the scalar projection of that mirror direction
vector onto the z-axis basis direction in the right-handed Cartesian
$(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame. The $\hat{z}$ basis direction is
vertical.

For mirror direction unit vector $\mathbf{u}$, the component is defined by:

$$
u_z = \mathbf{u}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}, \qquad \lVert\mathbf{u}\rVert = 1
$$

where $u_z$ is the z-axis component of the electron-cyclotron launcher
mirror direction unit vector, $\mathbf{u}$ is the unit vector defining that
mirror's translation direction or rotation axis at its home position,
$\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the positive z-axis basis vector in the right-handed
Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame, and $\lVert\mathbf{u}\rVert$
is the Euclidean norm of $\mathbf{u}$.

The quantity applies to an individual electron-cyclotron launcher mirror at
its home position. It is a single Cartesian component of the movement
direction or rotation axis, not an aggregate over launchers or mirrors and
not an average over a range of mirror motion.

It is not a mirror position, displacement, the vertical coordinate of a
point, or the angle of the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror. The
corresponding [x-axis
component](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror)
and [y-axis
component](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror)
complete the same home-position unit vector; with $u_x$ and $u_y$ denoting
those linked components, the components satisfy $u_x^2 + u_y^2 + u_z^2 = 1$.

items.name: surface_temperature
items.description:
Surface temperature is the thermodynamic temperature of the exposed material
boundary of a plasma-facing component at a specified surface point. It
refers to the surface material state, not to an area aggregate or regional
extremum.
items.documentation:
Surface temperature is the thermodynamic temperature of the material at the
exposed boundary of a plasma-facing component. It is a local scalar assigned
to a specified material surface point and time, representing the state of
the surface material rather than the temperature of the adjacent plasma,
sheath, neutral gas, or radiation field.

For an extended exposed surface, the unqualified quantity denotes the local
point value at each surface point, not an area average, integral,
percentile, or extremum. Region-level aggregates require distinct standard
names; the maximum over a specified exposed surface region is
[maximum_surface_temperature](name:maximum_surface_temperature).
[temperature_at_wall](name:temperature_at_wall) is the corresponding
boundary-locus temperature when the wall is the defining locus.

items.name: total_electron_pressure
items.description:
Total pressure of electrons is the isotropic kinetic stress from their
combined bulk thermal and nonthermal populations.
items.documentation:
Total pressure of electrons is the isotropic part of the kinetic pressure
tensor of the combined thermal and nonthermal electron populations. It
represents stress from random electron motion rather than bulk-flow momentum
flux and does not require an isotropic velocity distribution.

The total is defined by the additive population decomposition:

$$
p_e = p_{e,\mathrm{thermal}} + p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}
$$

where $p_e$ is the total electron pressure, $p_{e,\mathrm{thermal}}$ is the
bulk thermal-electron pressure, and $p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the
[fast-electron pressure](name:fast_electron_pressure), encompassing the
nonthermal contribution.

Both contributions must refer to the same plasma region and averaging
convention. For flux-surface-averaged core-plasma values, both are averaged
over the same magnetic flux surface. The aggregation is a direct sum, not a
density-weighted mean or a volume integral. It excludes ion pressure and
magnetic pressure and does not select a field-parallel or
field-perpendicular stress component.

This is the combined-population specialization of [electron
pressure](name:electron_pressure), whose broader definition also permits
thermal-only or suprathermal-only populations. It differs from either
population-specific pressure by explicitly including both contributions.

items.name: krypton_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron krypton source rate delivered to the
plasma vessel by gas injection systems, where each injected krypton atom
with Z = 36 contributes 36 equivalent-electron counts.
items.documentation:
The krypton source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous
rate at which neutral krypton with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} = 36$ is
admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count rate. Each neutral krypton atom contributes
$Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ equivalent electrons to the equivalent particle inventory;
this accounting uses nuclear charge and does not imply ionization at the
injection location.

The defining relation for krypton injection is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Kr}} = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}} = 36\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the krypton equivalent-electron source rate
in equivalent-electron counts per second, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the
neutral krypton atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}
= 36$ is the atomic number of krypton.

This is the krypton-species contribution to
[source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection)
and is the instantaneous time derivative of
[accumulated_krypton_count](name:accumulated_krypton_count) when the same
equivalent-electron accounting is used. It excludes krypton supplied by
mechanisms other than gas injection and differs from
gas_particle_source_rate_over_vessel_due_to_gas_injection, which is counted
as raw gas-phase particles rather than equivalent electrons. It is directly
parallel to same-family species quantities such as
[argon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:argon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection),
differing by the injected species and its atomic number.

items.name: ratio_of_neutral_density_of_isotope_to_difference_of_total_neutral_density_and_neutral_density_of_isotope
items.description:
Odds ratio of the neutral density of a selected hydrogen isotope to the
summed neutral density of all other hydrogen isotopes, distinguishing
composition odds from total isotope fraction.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the neutral-population odds ratio for one selected hydrogen
isotope relative to all other hydrogen isotopes. It characterizes isotope
composition using neutral atoms only, with the comparison population
aggregated across every other isotope.

$$
R_i = \frac{n_i}{\sum_{j \ne i} n_j}
$$

Here, $R_i$ is the isotope density ratio, $i$ identifies the selected
hydrogen isotope, $n_i$ is its neutral number density, and $n_j$ is the
neutral number density of another hydrogen isotope. The summation includes
all hydrogen isotopes other than the selected isotope.

The denominator is a total over the other neutral isotope populations, while
the numerator contains only the selected isotope. This quantity excludes
ionized populations and differs from
[total_hydrogenic_density](name:total_hydrogenic_density), which includes
the hydrogenic population across its applicable charge states and isotopes.
It is an odds ratio rather than the selected isotope's fraction of the total
neutral population; if $f_i$ denotes that corresponding neutral isotope
fraction, then $f_i = R_i/(1+R_i)$.

items.name: thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Signed local rate of Coulomb-collisional energy transfer from fast or
non-Maxwellian particles to thermal ions, summed over all ionic charge
states.
items.documentation:
Thermal-ion collisional power density is the signed local rate at which
Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from a designated fast or
non-Maxwellian particle population to thermal ions. It is an energy source
or sink for the thermal recipient population, not its stored kinetic-energy
density.

The exchange is defined by the kinetic-energy moment of the recipient
collision operator:

$$
P_{\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}}\sum_q \int \frac{1}{2}m_i|\mathbf{v}|^2 C_{iq,d}[f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}},f_d](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the thermal-ion collisional power
density, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is recipient velocity,
$\mathcal{I}$ is the included set of thermal-ion species, $i$ labels an ion
species, $q$ is its ionic charge number, and $m_i$ is its particle mass. The
function $f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal recipient distribution for
species $i$ and charge state $q$, $f_d$ is the designated donor
distribution, and $d$ labels the donor species. The operator $C_{iq,d}$
gives the collisional rate of change of the recipient distribution caused by
that donor; the integral covers recipient velocity space.

The quantity is summed over all ionic charge states of each included
species, with the species set comprising either one species or several. The
[charge-state-resolved thermal-ion collisional power
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions)
supplies an individual species-and-charge-state contribution. Contributions
from multiple designated donor distributions add. The quantity is locally
defined and is not intrinsically flux-surface averaged; a flux-surface
average represents the corresponding average of this local exchange.

This is the thermal-recipient contribution to [ion collisional power
density](name:ion_power_density_due_to_collisions), excluding energy
deposited into fast-ion or electron recipients. It includes all donor orbit
classes. Orbit-restricted quantities, such as [co-passing thermal-ion
collisional power
density](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions),
select the corresponding donor orbits. Summing co-passing, counter-passing,
and trapped contributions for the same recipients recovers the unrestricted
exchange; applying the same flux-surface average preserves this
decomposition.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy
from the designated donor population to the thermal ions.

items.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description:
Signed toroidal projection of the mass- and charge-independent E×B
guiding-center drift of one ion charge state in the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
The toroidal component of the [ion charge-state E×B drift
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is its
signed projection along the geometric toroidal direction. This direction
follows increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For the ideal E×B guiding-center drift, the defining projection is

$$
v_{E,\phi} = \mathbf{v}_E \cdot \hat{\phi} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\phi}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}.
$$

Here $v_{E,\phi}$ is the toroidal drift component for the specified ion
charge state, $\mathbf{v}_E$ is its E×B guiding-center drift velocity,
$\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic
field with magnitude $|\mathbf{B}|$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector
toward increasing toroidal angle. The definition requires a nonzero magnetic
field and the magnetized guiding-center regime. At fixed local fields, the
ideal drift is independent of ion mass and charge.

This quantity applies locally to one specified charge state of one ion
species in the edge plasma; it is neither summed nor averaged over charge
states or species. Other contributions to ion motion are excluded. It is a
linear velocity component, not a toroidal angle, angular velocity, or
drift-speed magnitude.

Unlike the [parallel
component](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift),
which vanishes identically for the ideal E×B drift, the toroidal projection
need not vanish: the geometric toroidal direction is not generally aligned
with the local magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when the E×B drift velocity has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: fast_ion_density
items.description:
Number density of fast, nonthermal ions of a specified species, summed over
all positive charge states and excluding thermal ions and neutral particles.
items.documentation:
Number density of ion

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{fast}} = \sum_{q>0} n_{i,q,\mathrm{fast}}
$$

where $i$ labels the selected ion species, $n_{i,\mathrm{fast}}$ is its
fast-ion number density, $q$ is the positive ionic charge number, and
$n_{i,q,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the [fast-ion charge-state
density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_density) for that species and charge
state.

The sum includes all positive charge states of the selected species, not
different ion species. Both trapped and passing fast ions are included.
Thermal ions and neutral particles are excluded, and the quantity is
distinct from electric charge density and mass density.

This is the fast-population contribution to [ion density](name:ion_density).
Adding the [thermal-ion density](name:thermal_ion_density) of the same
species gives its full ion number density when the thermal and fast
populations form a complete, nonoverlapping partition.
