items.name: poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_low_field_side
items.description:
Poloidal electron beta at the low-field-side pedestal top is the
dimensionless ratio of local electron thermal pressure to the local magnetic
pressure computed from the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude at the fitted
core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. Both quantities are
evaluated at the outboard, low-field-side point.
items.documentation:
Poloidal electron beta at the low-field-side pedestal top is the ratio of
local electron thermal pressure to the magnetic pressure computed from the
local poloidal magnetic-field magnitude at the fitted core-side shoulder of
the H-mode edge transport barrier. The low-field-side locus is the
outboard-midplane point, equivalently the largest-major-radius point on that
pedestal-top flux surface in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

The quantity is defined by the local pressure-to-field-pressure ratio at
that point:

$$
\beta_{e,\mathrm{pol,LFS}} = \frac{p_{e,\mathrm{ped,LFS}}}{B_{\mathrm{pol,ped,LFS}}^2/(2\mu_0)} = \frac{2\mu_0 p_{e,\mathrm{ped,LFS}}}{B_{\mathrm{pol,ped,LFS}}^2}
$$

where $p_{e,\mathrm{ped,LFS}}$ is the local electron pressure at the
low-field-side point of the pedestal-top surface, $B_{\mathrm{pol,ped,LFS}}$
is the local poloidal magnetic-field magnitude at the same point, and
$\mu_0$ is the vacuum permeability.

This is a point-local low-field-side beta: both the electron pressure and
the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude are evaluated at the same
low-field-side pedestal-top point. It differs from poloidal
flux-surface-averaged electron beta at the pedestal top, which uses
flux-surface averaging, from [poloidal electron beta at the high-field-side
pedestal top](name:poloidal_electron_beta_at_pedestal_top_high_field_side),
which uses the corresponding inboard point, and from [poloidal
beta](name:poloidal_beta), which uses a global plasma-pressure convention
rather than the local pedestal-top electron pressure.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_spectrometer_channel
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of an interpolated geometry point associated with a
spectrometer channel, measured from the toroidal symmetry axis in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the major-radius coordinate of an interpolated geometry
point associated with a spectrometer channel. It locates that point by its
perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

At each interpolated geometry point, the coordinate is defined from its
transverse Cartesian coordinates:

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2+y^2}
$$

where $R$ is the major-radius coordinate, and $x$ and $y$ are the Cartesian
coordinates along the $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{y}$ directions. The right-handed
Cartesian basis is $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$, with $\hat{z}$ equal to the
vertical unit direction $\hat{Z}$; in the cylindrical frame, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies pointwise to each interpolated geometry knot associated
with one spectrometer channel and is not summed, averaged, or integrated
over knots, channels, viewing paths, or plasma regions. It identifies a
geometry-point locus rather than a single radial location for the channel
body or a channel-wide average.

This is the spectrometer-channel-specific instance of the [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate). It retains the parent quantity's
major-radius definition while restricting its locus to an interpolated point
in the channel geometry.

items.name: normalized_gyrokinetic_time
items.description:
Dimensionless independent time coordinate that orders nonlinear gyrokinetic
evolution and indexes time-resolved turbulent fields, fluxes, and moments.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the dimensionless independent time coordinate for nonlinear
gyrokinetic evolution. It orders time-resolved turbulent fields, fluxes, and
velocity-space moments rather than representing a physical field or a
spatial coordinate.

The normalized time coordinate is defined by

$$
t_{\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{t}{t_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $t$ is the physical simulation time, $t_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the
positive reference time scale specified by the gyrokinetic normalization,
and $t_{\mathrm{norm}}$ is the resulting normalized time coordinate.

Its scope is the nonlinear gyrokinetic simulation timebase as a whole; it is
not assigned to a particle species, spatial region, mode, or diagnostic
channel. It is a coordinate rather than an averaged, integrated, or
charge-state-aggregated quantity, and it is distinct from an interval
between two time instants or from the unnormalized physical time coordinate.

Differences between two values of this coordinate define normalized time
intervals used to parameterize temporal evolution. Unlike [normalized
particle perturbed energy](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_energy), which
is a normalized velocity-space moment, this quantity is the independent
temporal coordinate against which such moments and turbulent fluxes are
resolved.

items.name: deuterium_tritium_power_density_due_to_fusion
items.description:
Local volumetric rate of energy release from deuterium-tritium thermonuclear
reactions, including energy carried by the alpha-particle and neutron
products and characterized by the D-T channel Q value.
items.documentation:
The D-T fusion power density is the local rate at which deuterium-tritium
thermonuclear reactions release energy per unit plasma volume. It includes
the birth energy of both reaction products, the alpha particle and the
neutron, through the D-T channel energy release.

The defining reaction-rate expression is

$$
P_{\mathrm{DT}}(\mathbf{x}) = n_D(\mathbf{x})\,n_T(\mathbf{x})\,\langle\sigma v\rangle_{\mathrm{DT}}\,E_{\mathrm{DT}}
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $P_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is D-T fusion
power density, $n_D$ is deuterium reactant number density, $n_T$ is tritium
reactant number density, $\langle\sigma v\rangle_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the
reaction-rate coefficient for deuterium-tritium fusion, and
$E_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the total energy released per deuterium-tritium
reaction.

It is defined locally for plasma containing deuterium and tritium reactants
and has no spatial aggregation: line-integrated, flux-surface-averaged,
volume-integrated, and total fusion power quantities are distinct. It is
channel-specific, so it excludes deuterium-deuterium and other fusion
reaction channels, and it is not the local deposited heating power from
alpha particles or neutrons after they are born.

Deuterium-tritium fusion power density is the D-T channel contribution to
[fusion power density](name:power_density_due_to_fusion); a channel-summed
fusion power density adds it to other included channel contributions such as
[deuterium-deuterium fusion power
density](name:deuterium_deuterium_power_density_due_to_fusion). Because each
deuterium-tritium reaction produces one neutron, [D-T fusion
emissivity](name:deuterium_tritium_emissivity_due_to_fusion) is the
corresponding reaction-rate density, and multiplying that emissivity by
$E_{\mathrm{DT}}$ gives the D-T fusion power density.

items.name: radial_offset_of_beamlet_group
items.description:
Signed major-radius displacement of a beamlet-group center from its nominal
position, measured along the radial direction in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the signed radial displacement of a beamlet-group center
from its nominal static position during a position variation. It describes
only the major-radius component of the group's displacement, not the
complete position vector or the injector's own reference position.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ frame, the
offset is defined by:

$$
\Delta R_{\mathrm{bg}} = R_{\mathrm{bg}} - R_{\mathrm{bg},0}
$$

Here $R_{\mathrm{bg}}$ is the beamlet-group center's major-radius coordinate
and $R_{\mathrm{bg},0}$ is its nominal static reference coordinate; $R$ is
measured from the machine symmetry axis and increases outward.

For dynamic beam tilting, the offset describes the group's positional
variation and is distinct from the [radial coordinate of the neutral beam
injector](name:radial_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector), which refers to
the injector reference position. Related angular variation is described by
the perturbed beam tilt angle of the neutral beam injector.

Sign convention: Positive when the beamlet-group center lies at larger major
radius than its nominal reference position.

items.name: toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged rate of toroidal angular-momentum transfer per volume
from counter-passing fast particles to thermal ions of one specified charge
state through Coulomb collisions.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged torque per unit plasma volume
delivered to thermal ions of one specified species and charge state through
Coulomb collisions with counter-passing fast particles. It represents
angular-momentum transfer associated with rotation about the symmetry axis.

The defining relation is

$$
\mathcal{T}_\phi = \left\langle R F_{\phi,\mathrm{cp,coll}} \right\rangle
$$

where $\mathcal{T}_\phi$ is this averaged toroidal torque density, $R$ is
the major radius, and $F_{\phi,\mathrm{cp,coll}}$ is the toroidal
collisional force density acting on the specified thermal ion charge state
through interactions with counter-passing fast particles. The labels
$\mathrm{cp}$ and $\mathrm{coll}$ identify the counter-passing contribution
and Coulomb collisions, respectively. Angle brackets denote flux-surface
averaging with differential-volume weighting. The toroidal direction is
toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $Z$ is vertical height.

The counter-passing restriction applies to the contributing fast-particle
distribution, not to the receiving thermal-ion orbits. The receiving
population is restricted to one specified ionic charge state; no sum over
charge states is taken. Unlike [toroidal counter-passing fast-ion
charge-state torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
this quantity describes transfer to thermal rather than fast ions.

It is the flux-surface-averaged toroidal specialization of [counter-passing
thermal ion charge-state torque density due to
collisions](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
within the broader [torque-density](name:torque_density) family of
angular-momentum source densities. The average remains a torque density and
is not a volume-integrated torque.

Sign convention: Positive when the net collisional transfer increases the
receiving thermal ions' angular momentum for rotation toward increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: square_of_ion_charge_state_charge_number
items.description:
Concentration-weighted mean of squared ionic charge numbers within one
charge-state bundle of one ion species, distinct from the square of its mean
charge number.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the concentration-weighted second moment of the ionic
charge-number distribution in one charge-state bundle of one ion species. It
averages squared charge numbers within the bundle rather than squaring their
mean.

The bundle's mean squared charge number is defined by

$$
\langle Z^2\rangle_{\mathcal B} = \sum_{Z\in\mathcal B} Z^2 x_Z
$$

where $\mathcal B$ is the specified bundle of charge states, $Z$ is the
ionic charge number, $x_Z$ is the relative number concentration of charge
state $Z$ within the bundle, and $\langle Z^2\rangle_{\mathcal B}$ is the
resulting second moment. The concentrations satisfy $\sum_{Z\in\mathcal
B}x_Z=1$.

Only charge states belonging to the specified bundle contribute; other
bundles and other ion species are excluded. For an unbundled, single charge
state, the result is $Z_{\min}^2$, where $Z_{\min}$ is the bundle's minimum
charge number. Charge-state averaging is distinct from spatial averaging: a
plasma-volume-averaged form additionally averages this moment with
physical-volume weighting over the plasma radius.

This is the second-moment specialization of [ion charge-state charge
number](name:ion_charge_state_charge_number). It exceeds the square of the
[bundle's mean charge number](name:ion_charge_state_average_charge_number)
by the charge-number variance, with equality for a single populated charge
state. The related [species-level mean squared charge
number](name:square_of_ion_charge_number) instead includes all charge states
of the ion species.

items.name: thermal_electron_pressure_at_post_sawtooth_crash
items.description:
Pressure of thermal electrons at the post-sawtooth-crash locus is the
isotropic stress from random electron motion in the plasma edge and
scrape-off layer.
items.documentation:
Pressure of electron at post sawtooth crash

The pressure is defined by the isotropic second central velocity moment:

$$
p_e = \frac{m_e}{3}\int |\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_e|^2 f_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_e$ is the thermal electron pressure, $m_e$ is the electron mass,
$\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, $\mathbf{u}_e$ is the mean velocity of
the thermal electron population, $f_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is its velocity
distribution whose integral equals the thermal-electron number density, and
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integral extends over
velocity space for the thermal population only.

This quantity includes only thermal electrons, not a sum over plasma
species. It excludes fast and other nonthermal electron contributions, ion
pressure, and stress from directed bulk motion. It is an isotropic pressure
rather than a field-parallel or field-perpendicular tensor component.

It supplies the electron contribution to [thermal plasma
pressure](name:thermal_plasma_pressure), which also includes thermal-ion
contributions. At the same evaluation locus, [total electron
pressure](name:total_electron_pressure) is the additive combination of this
thermal contribution and any nonthermal electron pressure.
